artificer.name: Artificer
artificer.description: A master of magical invention, blending magic and craftsmanship into devices no one else could build. You arm your party with infusions and gadgets, and solve problems with a tool you made yourself.
toolProficiencies: One type of artisan's tools of your choice
features: Tinker's Magic - You can create a mundane item with your tinker's tools, a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier per long rest
Spellcasting - You can cast artificer spells using Intelligence as your spellcasting ability
Replicate Magic Item - You learn plans for magic items and create them at the end of a long rest, up to your level's limit
The Right Tool for the Job - You can create artisan's tools with 1 hour of work

subclasses.name: Alchemist
subclasses.description: Master of potions and experimental elixirs

3.name: Tool Proficiency
3.description: You gain proficiency with alchemist's supplies. If you already have this proficiency, you gain proficiency with one other type of artisan's tools of your choice.

3.name: Alchemist Spells
3.description: You always have certain spells prepared based on your artificer level. These spells count as artificer spells for you but don't count against your number of prepared spells.

3.name: Experimental Elixir
3.description: When you finish a long rest, you can magically produce one experimental elixir in an empty flask you touch. Roll on the Experimental Elixir table or choose the effect. As an action, a creature can drink the elixir or administer it. Creating an elixir requires a 1st-level spell slot. Effects: Healing (2d4+Int HP), Swiftness (+10 speed for 1 hour), Resilience (+1 AC for 10 minutes), Boldness (1d4 to attack and saves for 1 minute), Flight (10 ft flying for 10 minutes), Transformation (alter self for 10 minutes). Elixirs last until your next long rest.

5.name: Alchemical Savant
5.description: When you cast a spell using your alchemist's supplies as the spellcasting focus, you gain a bonus to one roll of the spell. That roll must restore HP or deal acid, fire, necrotic, or poison damage. The bonus equals your Intelligence modifier (minimum +1).

9.name: Restorative Reagents
9.description: You can cast Lesser Restoration without expending a spell slot, doing so a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum once). You regain all uses when you finish a long rest. Additionally, when a creature drinks an Experimental Elixir you created, the creature gains temporary HP equal to 2d6 + your Intelligence modifier.

15.name: Chemical Mastery
15.description: You have resistance to acid and poison damage, and you are immune to the poisoned condition. You can cast Greater Restoration and Heal without expending a spell slot, without having the spell prepared, and without providing the material component. Once you cast either spell with this feature, you can't cast that spell again until you finish a long rest.

subclasses.name: Armorer
subclasses.description: Magical armor specialist who becomes one with their suit

3.name: Tools of the Trade
3.description: You gain proficiency with heavy armor and smith's tools. If you already have a proficiency, you gain proficiency with another artisan's tool of your choice.

3.name: Armorer Spells
3.description: You always have certain spells prepared based on your artificer level. These count as artificer spells for you but don't count against your prepared spells.

3.name: Arcane Armor
3.description: As an action, you turn a suit of armor into Arcane Armor. It expands to cover your entire body, you can use it as a spellcasting focus, it attaches armor gauntlets, the armor can't be removed against your will, it replaces missing limbs, and you ignore Strength requirements.

3.name: Armor Model
3.description: Choose a model: Guardian (Thunder Gauntlets: melee 1d8 thunder, target has disadvantage attacking others; Defensive Field: gain temp HP equal to artificer level as bonus action, uses = proficiency bonus per long rest) or Infiltrator (Lightning Launcher: ranged 90ft 1d6 lightning, +1d6 once per turn; 5 ft walking speed boost; advantage on Stealth). You can change model on short or long rest.

5.name: Extra Attack
5.description: You can attack twice, rather than once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

9.name: Armor Modifications
9.description: Your Arcane Armor now counts as separate items for infusion purposes: armor (chest), boots, helmet, and the armor's special weapon. Each piece can bear one of your infusions, and the infusions transfer when you change armor. You can also infuse a new item with no limit to how many items you can infuse at once.

15.name: Perfected Armor
15.description: Guardian gains Perfected: when a Huge or smaller creature you can see ends its turn within 30 feet, you can use your reaction to magically force it to make a Strength save. On failure, pull it up to 30 feet toward you, and if it ends within 5 feet, deal lightning damage equal to your Intelligence modifier. Infiltrator gains Perfected: any creature that takes lightning damage from your Lightning Launcher glimmers until the start of your next turn. While glimmering, it can't benefit from invisibility, and the next attack against it has advantage.

subclasses.name: Artillerist
subclasses.description: Master of magical cannons and explosives

3.name: Tool Proficiency
3.description: You gain proficiency with woodcarver's tools. If you already have this proficiency, you gain proficiency with one other type of artisan's tools of your choice.

3.name: Artillerist Spells
3.description: You always have certain spells prepared based on your artificer level. These count as artificer spells for you but don't count against your prepared spells.

3.name: Eldritch Cannon
3.description: As an action, you create a Small or Tiny magical cannon in an unoccupied space within 5 feet. It has AC 18 and HP equal to 5× your artificer level. It is immune to poison and psychic damage. Choose its type when created: Flamethrower (15 ft cone, Dex save, 2d8 fire), Force Ballista (ranged attack, 2d8 force, push 5 ft), or Protector (10 ft radius, 1d8+Int temp HP). Activate as bonus action; lasts 1 hour. You can create one cannon for free per long rest; additional cannons cost a spell slot.

5.name: Arcane Firearm
5.description: Using woodcarver's tools, you turn a wand, staff, or rod into an arcane firearm, your spellcasting focus. When you cast an artificer spell through the firearm, roll a d8 and add the result to one of the spell's damage rolls.

9.name: Explosive Cannon
9.description: Your Eldritch Cannon's damage increases: Flamethrower deals 3d8 fire, Force Ballista deals 3d8 force. Additionally, as an action, you can command the cannon to detonate. Each creature within 20 feet makes a Dex save, taking 3d8 force damage on a failed save (half on success). The cannon is destroyed.

15.name: Fortified Position
15.description: You and your allies have half cover while within 10 feet of an Eldritch Cannon you created. You can now have two cannons at the same time. If you create a third, one you choose is destroyed. Activating both uses a single bonus action, and each can be a different type.

subclasses.name: Battle Smith
subclasses.description: Warrior artificer with a mechanical companion

3.name: Tool Proficiency
3.description: You gain proficiency with smith's tools. If you already have this proficiency, you gain proficiency with one other type of artisan's tools of your choice.

3.name: Battle Smith Spells
3.description: You always have certain spells prepared based on your artificer level. These count as artificer spells for you but don't count against your prepared spells.

3.name: Battle Ready
3.description: You gain proficiency with martial weapons. When you attack with a magic weapon, you can use your Intelligence modifier instead of Strength or Dexterity for the attack and damage rolls.

3.name: Steel Defender
3.description: You create a Steel Defender, a loyal construct that accompanies you. It uses your proficiency bonus, has HP equal to 5× your artificer level + your Int modifier + the defender's Con modifier × your artificer level. In combat, it shares your initiative and takes its turn immediately after yours. It can take the Dodge action on its own, but requires your bonus action to command it to take another action (Attack, Dash, Disengage, Help, or Repair - 2d8+proficiency HP healed). If it dies, you can revive it after 1 minute or create a new one during a long rest.

5.name: Extra Attack
5.description: You can attack twice, rather than once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

9.name: Arcane Jolt
9.description: Your magic strikes and your Steel Defender become more powerful. When you or your Steel Defender hits with a magic weapon attack or the defender's Force-Empowered Rend, you can channel magical energy to cause extra effects. The target takes an extra 2d6 force damage, OR one creature or object you choose within 30 feet of the target regains 2d6 hit points. You can use this a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum once) per long rest.

15.name: Improved Defender
15.description: Your Arcane Jolt damage and healing increase to 4d6. Your Steel Defender gains a +2 bonus to AC. Additionally, when your Steel Defender uses its Deflect Attack reaction, the attacker takes force damage equal to 1d4 + your Intelligence modifier.

subclasses.name: Cartographer
subclasses.description: Premier navigator and reconnaissance agent who charts courses through turmoil

3.description: You gain proficiency with calligrapher's supplies and cartographer's tools. If you already have one of these proficiencies, you gain proficiency with one other type of artisan's tools of your choice (or two other types if you have both).
3.name: Tool Proficiency

3.description: You always have certain spells prepared based on your artificer level. These spells count as artificer spells for you but don't count against your number of prepared spells.
3.name: Cartographer Spells

3.description: Whenever you finish a long rest while holding cartographer's tools, you can create a set of magical maps by touching at least two creatures (up to 1 + your Intelligence modifier, minimum two). Each map holder adds 1d4 to Initiative rolls and knows the location of all other map holders on the same plane, and can target another map holder with a spell or effect regardless of sight or cover, so long as the target is within range.
3.name: Adventurer's Atlas

3.description: Illuminated Cartography: you can cast Faerie Fire without expending a spell slot a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum once) per long rest. Portal Jump: on your turn, you can spend movement equal to half your speed (rounded down) to teleport to an unoccupied space you can see within 10 feet of yourself or within 5 feet of a creature within 30 feet of you that holds one of your maps.
3.name: Mapping Magic

5.description: Once per turn, when you cast a spell from your Cartographer Spells list or hit a creature affected by your Faerie Fire with an attack roll, you can add your Intelligence modifier to one damage roll of the spell or attack. Taking damage can't cause you to lose concentration on Faerie Fire.
5.name: Guided Precision

9.description: When you use your Flash of Genius, you or a willing creature you can see within 30 feet of yourself can teleport up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space you can see as part of that same reaction.
9.name: Ingenious Movement

15.description: Your Adventurer's Atlas improves. Safe Haven: when a map holder would be reduced to 0 hit points but not killed outright, it can destroy its map; its hit points instead become twice your artificer level, and it teleports to an unoccupied space within 5 feet of you or another map holder of its choice. Unerring Path: if you are one of the map holders, you can cast Find the Path without expending a spell slot, without preparing it, and without needing spell components, once per long rest.
15.name: Superior Atlas

barbarian.name: Barbarian
barbarian.description: A fierce warrior who fights with raw fury, shrugging off blows that would kill anyone else. When you rage, you hit harder, endure longer, and become the wall between your party and everything trying to kill them.
features: Rage - In battle, you fight with primal ferocity. Gain bonus damage and resistance to physical damage
Unarmored Defense - While not wearing armor, your AC equals 10 + DEX modifier + CON modifier

subclasses.name: Path of the Berserker
subclasses.description: Channel rage into violent fury

3.name: Frenzy
3.description: You can go into a frenzy when you rage. If you do so, for the duration of your rage you can make a single melee weapon attack as a bonus action on each of your turns after this one. When your rage ends, you suffer one level of exhaustion.

6.name: Mindless Rage
6.description: You can't be charmed or frightened while raging. If you are charmed or frightened when you enter your rage, the effect is suspended for the duration of the rage.

10.name: Intimidating Presence
10.description: You can use your action to frighten someone with your menacing presence. Choose one creature you can see within 30 feet. If the creature can see or hear you, it must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw (DC equal to 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Charisma modifier) or be frightened of you until the end of your next turn. On subsequent turns, you can use your action to extend the duration of this effect on the frightened creature until the end of your next turn.

14.name: Retaliation
14.description: When you take damage from a creature that is within 5 feet of you, you can use your reaction to make a melee weapon attack against that creature.

subclasses.name: Path of the Totem Warrior
subclasses.description: Draw upon animal spirits for power

3.name: Spirit Seeker
3.description: You gain the ability to cast Beast Sense and Speak with Animals spells, but only as rituals.

3.name: Totem Spirit
3.description: Choose a totem spirit. Bear: While raging, you have resistance to all damage except psychic damage. Eagle: While raging, other creatures have disadvantage on opportunity attack rolls against you, and you can take the Dash action as a bonus action. Wolf: While raging, your friends have advantage on melee attack rolls against any creature within 5 feet of you that is hostile to you.

6.name: Aspect of the Beast
6.description: Choose an aspect. Bear: Your carrying capacity doubles, and you have advantage on Strength checks made to push, pull, lift, or break objects. Eagle: You can see up to 1 mile away with no difficulty, and no disadvantage on Perception checks at long distances. Wolf: You can track other creatures while traveling at a fast pace, and you can move stealthily while traveling at a normal pace.

10.name: Spirit Walker
10.description: You can cast the Commune with Nature spell, but only as a ritual. When you do so, a spiritual version of one of the animals you chose for Totem Spirit or Aspect of the Beast appears to you to convey the information you seek.

14.name: Totemic Attunement
14.description: Choose an attunement. Bear: While raging, any creature within 5 feet of you that's hostile to you has disadvantage on attack rolls against targets other than you. Eagle: While raging, you have a flying speed equal to your current walking speed. Wolf: While raging, you can use a bonus action to knock a Large or smaller creature prone when you hit it with a melee weapon attack.

subclasses.name: Path of the Ancestral Guardian
subclasses.description: Call upon ancestor spirits to protect allies

3.name: Ancestral Protectors
3.description: Spectral warriors appear when you enter your rage. The first creature you hit with an attack on your turn becomes the target of the warriors, which hinder its attacks. Until the start of your next turn, that target has disadvantage on any attack roll that isn't against you, and when the target hits a creature other than you with an attack, that creature has resistance to the damage dealt by the attack.

6.name: Spirit Shield
6.description: If you are raging and another creature you can see within 30 feet of you takes damage, you can use your reaction to reduce that damage by 2d6. At 10th level, the reduction increases to 3d6, and at 14th level to 4d6.

10.name: Consult the Spirits
10.description: You can cast Augury or Clairvoyance, without using a spell slot or material components. Your spell save DC for these spells equals 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Wisdom modifier. Once you cast either spell in this way, you can't use this feature again until you finish a short or long rest.

14.name: Vengeful Ancestors
14.description: Your ancestral spirits grow powerful enough to retaliate. When you use your Spirit Shield to reduce the damage of an attack, the attacker takes an amount of force damage equal to the damage that your Spirit Shield prevents.

subclasses.name: Path of the Storm Herald
subclasses.description: Channel elemental fury in an aura

3.name: Storm Aura
3.description: You emanate a stormy, magical aura while you rage. The aura extends 10 feet from you in every direction, but not through total cover. Your aura has an effect that activates when you enter your rage, and you can activate the effect again on each of your turns as a bonus action. Choose an environment: Desert (each creature of your choice in your aura takes 2 fire damage), Sea (you can choose one creature in your aura; it must make a Dexterity save or take 1d6 lightning damage), or Tundra (each creature of your choice in your aura gains 2 temporary hit points).

6.name: Storm Soul
6.description: The storm grants you benefits even when your aura isn't active. Desert: You have resistance to fire damage, and you don't suffer the effects of extreme heat. Sea: You have resistance to lightning damage, you can breathe underwater, and you have a swimming speed of 30 feet. Tundra: You have resistance to cold damage, and you don't suffer the effects of extreme cold.

10.name: Shielding Storm
10.description: You learn to use your mastery of the storm to protect others. Each creature of your choice has the damage resistance you gained from the Storm Soul feature while the creature is in your Storm Aura.

14.name: Raging Storm
14.description: The power of the storm you channel grows mightier. Desert: Immediately after a creature in your aura hits you with an attack, you can use your reaction to force that creature to make a Dexterity save. On a failed save, the creature takes fire damage equal to half your barbarian level. Sea: When you hit a creature in your aura with an attack, you can use your reaction to force that creature to make a Strength save or be knocked prone. Tundra: Whenever the effect of your Storm Aura is activated, you can choose one creature you can see in the aura. That creature must succeed on a Strength save, or its speed is reduced to 0 until the start of your next turn.

subclasses.name: Path of the Zealot
subclasses.description: Warrior fueled by divine fury

3.name: Divine Fury
3.description: While you're raging, the first creature you hit on each of your turns with a weapon attack takes extra damage equal to 1d6 + half your barbarian level. The extra damage is necrotic or radiant (your choice when you gain this feature).

3.name: Warrior of the Gods
3.description: Your soul is marked for endless battle. If a spell, such as Raise Dead, has the sole effect of restoring you to life (but not undeath), the caster doesn't need material components to cast the spell on you.

6.name: Fanatical Focus
6.description: If you fail a saving throw while raging, you can reroll it, and you must use the new roll. You can use this ability only once per rage.

10.name: Zealous Presence
10.description: You can channel divine power to inspire zealotry in others. As a bonus action, you unleash a battle cry infused with divine energy. Up to ten other creatures of your choice within 60 feet of you that can hear you gain advantage on attack rolls and saving throws until the start of your next turn. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest.

14.name: Rage Beyond Death
14.description: While you're raging, having 0 hit points doesn't knock you unconscious. You still must make death saving throws, and you suffer the normal effects of taking damage while at 0 hit points. However, if you would die due to failing death saving throws, you don't die until your rage ends, and you die then only if you still have 0 hit points.

subclasses.name: Path of the Beast
subclasses.description: Transform into a bestial form when raging

3.name: Form of the Beast
3.description: When you enter your rage, you can transform, revealing the bestial power within you. Until the rage ends, you manifest a natural weapon: Bite (1d8 piercing, regain HP equal to your proficiency bonus once per turn when you damage a creature at less than half your max HP), Claws (1d6 slashing each, can make one additional claw attack when you take the Attack action), or Tail (1d8 piercing, 10-foot reach, can use reaction to add 1d8 to your AC against one attack).

6.name: Bestial Soul
6.description: The feral power within you increases. Your natural weapons count as magical. You can also alter your form to help you adapt to your surroundings. When you finish a short or long rest, choose one benefit: swimming speed equal to your walking speed and breathe underwater, climbing speed equal to your walking speed and climb difficult surfaces, or extend your jump distance by feet equal to your ability check.

10.name: Infectious Fury
10.description: When you hit a creature with your natural weapons while raging, the beast within you can curse your target with rabid fury. The target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw (DC equal to 8 + your Constitution modifier + your proficiency bonus) or suffer one of the following effects (your choice): The target must use its reaction to make a melee attack against another creature of your choice, or the target takes 2d12 psychic damage. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus.

14.name: Call the Hunt
14.description: When you enter your rage, you can choose a number of other willing creatures you can see within 30 feet of you equal to your Constitution modifier (minimum of one creature). You gain 5 temporary hit points for each creature that accepts this feature. Until the rage ends, the chosen creatures can use a d6 each time they deal damage with an attack.

subclasses.name: Path of Wild Magic
subclasses.description: Channel raw magical energy through rage

3.name: Magic Awareness
3.description: As an action, you can open your awareness to the presence of concentrated magic. Until the end of your next turn, you know the location of any spell or magic item within 60 feet of you that isn't behind total cover. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus.

3.name: Wild Surge
3.description: When you enter your rage, roll on the Wild Magic table to determine the magical effect produced. The effect lasts for the duration of your rage, unless otherwise specified.

6.name: Bolstering Magic
6.description: You can harness your wild magic to bolster yourself or a companion. As an action, you can touch one creature (which can be yourself) and confer one of the following benefits of your choice: For 10 minutes, the creature can roll a d3 whenever making an attack roll or ability check and add the number rolled to the d20 roll, or roll a d3. The creature regains one expended spell slot, the level of which equals the number rolled or lower (creature's choice). Once a creature receives this benefit, that creature can't receive it again until after a long rest.

10.name: Unstable Backlash
10.description: When you are imperiled during your rage, the magic within you can lash out. Immediately after you take damage or fail a saving throw while raging, you can use your reaction to roll on the Wild Magic table and immediately produce the effect rolled. This effect replaces your current Wild Magic effect.

14.name: Controlled Surge
14.description: Whenever you roll on the Wild Magic table, you can roll the die twice and choose which of the two effects to unleash. If you roll the same number on both dice, you can ignore the number and choose any effect on the table.

subclasses.name: Path of the Mountain
subclasses.description: Barbarians who follow this path draw strength from the mountains themselves, becoming as immovable and enduring as stone

3.name: Mountain Stance
3.description: While raging, you can root yourself to the ground as a bonus action. Until the start of your next turn, you can't be moved against your will, you have advantage on Strength checks and saving throws, and any creature that hits you with a melee attack takes bludgeoning damage equal to your Constitution modifier.

3.name: Stone's Endurance
3.description: You can focus yourself to occasionally shrug off injury. When you take damage, you can use your reaction to roll a d12. Add your Constitution modifier to the number rolled, and reduce the damage by that total. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus.

6.name: Avalanche Strike
6.description: While raging, once per turn when you hit a creature with a melee weapon attack, you can force that creature to make a Strength saving throw (DC equal to 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Strength modifier). On a failed save, the creature is knocked prone and takes additional bludgeoning damage equal to your rage damage bonus.

10.name: Heart of the Mountain
10.description: You gain resistance to cold damage. Additionally, while raging, you have resistance to all damage except psychic damage (this replaces the normal rage resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage). You also ignore difficult terrain.

14.name: Living Landslide
14.description: While raging, as an action, you can move up to your speed in a straight line. Each creature in your path must make a Dexterity saving throw (DC equal to 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Strength modifier). On a failed save, a creature takes 4d10 bludgeoning damage and is knocked prone. On a successful save, the creature takes half damage and isn't knocked prone. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

subclasses.name: Path of the Witch Hunter
subclasses.description: Barbarians who dedicate themselves to hunting down spellcasters and destroying dark magic wherever they find it

3.name: Spell Warding
3.description: While raging, when you fail a saving throw against a spell that deals damage, you can reroll the save. You must use the new roll. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus per long rest.

6.name: Witch Sense
6.description: You can use your Charisma modifier instead of Intelligence for Investigation checks. As a bonus action, you can sense the presence of invisible or hidden creatures within 15 feet of you until the end of your next turn. You can use this sense a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus per long rest.

10.name: Magical Resistance
10.description: While raging, you have resistance to damage dealt by spells. Additionally, you have advantage on saving throws against being charmed or frightened by magical effects.

14.name: Witch's Bane
14.description: While raging, you gain proficiency in Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma saving throws if you don't already have it. When a creature within 5 feet of you attempts to teleport or cast a spell, you can use your reaction to make a melee weapon attack against it. If the attack hits, the creature must make a Constitution save (DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Strength modifier) or the teleport or spell fails and is wasted.

subclasses.name: Path of the Dragon
subclasses.description: Barbarians who channel ancient draconic power, transforming into fearsome dragon-blooded warriors when they rage

3.name: Draconic Transformation
3.description: When you enter your rage, you can transform with draconic power. Choose a dragon color (which determines your elemental damage type: red/gold = fire, white/silver = cold, blue/bronze = lightning, black/copper = acid, green = poison). While raging in this form, you gain natural weapons: claws (1d4 slashing + elemental damage), a tail (1d8 bludgeoning, reach 10 ft), and a bite (1d10 piercing). You can use a bonus action to make one unarmed strike with your natural weapons.

6.name: Unleashed Savagery
6.description: Your natural weapon attacks count as magical for the purpose of overcoming resistance and immunity. Additionally, you gain a breath weapon: as an action while raging, you exhale destructive energy in a 15-foot cone. Each creature in the area must make a Dexterity saving throw (DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Strength modifier), taking 6d6 damage of your chosen elemental type on a failed save, or half on a success. You can use this once per rage.

10.name: Dragonhide
10.description: You gain permanent resistance to the elemental damage type of your chosen dragon color. While raging, your scales harden — you gain resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical attacks (this replaces the normal rage resistance).

14.name: Tyrant of the Skies
14.description: When you enter your rage, you can manifest dragon wings. While raging, you gain a flying speed equal to your walking speed (you cannot fly in heavy armor). Your breath weapon damage increases to 8d6, and you can use it twice per rage. Additionally, while flying, you can use your action to perform a Diving Strike: move at least 20 feet straight toward a creature and make a melee attack. On a hit, the attack deals an extra 4d6 damage of your elemental type.

bard.name: Bard
bard.description: A performer whose music, stories, and wit carry real magic. You lift your allies, cut your enemies down with a word, and talk your way through doors that swords can't open.
toolProficiencies: Three musical instruments of your choice
features: Spellcasting - You can cast bard spells using Charisma as your spellcasting ability
Bardic Inspiration - You can inspire others through stirring words or music

subclasses.name: College of Lore
subclasses.description: Master of knowledge and secrets

3.name: Bonus Proficiencies
3.description: You gain proficiency with three skills of your choice.

3.name: Cutting Words
3.description: When a creature that you can see within 60 feet of you makes an attack roll, an ability check, or a damage roll, you can use your reaction to expend one of your uses of Bardic Inspiration, rolling a Bardic Inspiration die and subtracting the number rolled from the creature's roll. You can choose to use this feature after the creature makes its roll, but before the DM determines whether the attack roll or ability check succeeds or fails, or before the creature deals its damage.

6.name: Additional Magical Secrets
6.description: You learn two spells of your choice from any class. A spell you choose must be of a level you can cast, or a cantrip. The chosen spells count as bard spells for you but don't count against the number of bard spells you know.

14.name: Peerless Skill
14.description: When you make an ability check, you can expend one use of Bardic Inspiration. Roll a Bardic Inspiration die and add the number rolled to your ability check. You can choose to do so after you roll the die for the ability check, but before the DM tells you whether you succeed or fail.

subclasses.name: College of Valor
subclasses.description: Warrior poet who inspires allies in combat

3.name: Bonus Proficiencies
3.description: You gain proficiency with medium armor, shields, and martial weapons.

3.name: Combat Inspiration
3.description: A creature that has a Bardic Inspiration die from you can roll that die and add the number rolled to a weapon damage roll it just made. Alternatively, when an attack roll is made against the creature, it can use its reaction to roll the Bardic Inspiration die and add the number rolled to its AC against that attack.

6.name: Extra Attack
6.description: You can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

14.name: Battle Magic
14.description: When you use your action to cast a bard spell, you can make one weapon attack as a bonus action.

subclasses.name: College of Glamour
subclasses.description: Beguiling performer who uses fey magic

3.name: Mantle of Inspiration
3.description: As a bonus action, you can expend one use of your Bardic Inspiration to grant yourself a wondrous appearance. When you do so, choose a number of creatures you can see and who can see you within 60 feet of you, up to a number equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of one). Each of them gains 5 temporary hit points. When a creature gains these temporary hit points, it can immediately use its reaction to move up to its speed, without provoking opportunity attacks. The number of temporary hit points increases when you reach certain levels: 8 at 5th level, 11 at 10th level, and 14 at 15th level.

3.name: Enthralling Performance
3.description: You can charge your performance with seductive, fey magic. If you perform for at least 1 minute, you can attempt to inspire wonder in your audience. At the end of the performance, choose a number of humanoids within 60 feet of you who watched and listened to all of it, up to a number equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of one). Each target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or be charmed by you.

6.name: Mantle of Majesty
6.description: You gain the ability to cloak yourself in a fey magic that makes others want to serve you. As a bonus action, you cast Command, without expending a spell slot, and you take on an appearance of unearthly beauty for 1 minute or until your concentration ends. During this time, you can cast Command as a bonus action on each of your turns, without expending a spell slot. Any creature charmed by you automatically fails its saving throw against the Command you cast with this feature.

14.name: Unbreakable Majesty
14.description: You gain an otherworldly aspect to your appearance that makes you look more lovely and fierce. As a bonus action, you can assume a magically majestic presence for 1 minute or until you are incapacitated. For the duration, whenever any creature tries to attack you for the first time on a turn, the attacker must make a Charisma saving throw. On a failed save, it can't attack you on this turn, and it must choose a new target for its attack or the attack is wasted. On a successful save, it can attack you on this turn, but it has disadvantage on any saving throw it makes against your spells on your next turn.

subclasses.name: College of Swords
subclasses.description: Blade master who combines steel and song

3.name: Bonus Proficiencies
3.description: You gain proficiency with medium armor and the scimitar. If you're proficient with a simple or martial melee weapon, you can use it as a spellcasting focus for your bard spells.

3.name: Fighting Style
3.description: Choose a fighting style: Dueling (+2 damage with one-handed melee weapon when no other weapon) or Two-Weapon Fighting (add ability modifier to off-hand damage).

3.name: Blade Flourish
3.description: Whenever you take the Attack action on your turn, your walking speed increases by 10 feet until the end of the turn, and if a weapon attack that you make as part of this action hits a creature, you can use one of the following Blade Flourish options of your choice. You can use only one Blade Flourish option per turn: Defensive Flourish, Slashing Flourish, or Mobile Flourish.

6.name: Extra Attack
6.description: You can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

14.name: Master's Flourish
14.description: Whenever you use a Blade Flourish option, you can roll a d6 and use it instead of expending a Bardic Inspiration die.

subclasses.name: College of Whispers
subclasses.description: Master of fear and manipulation

3.name: Psychic Blades
3.description: When you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can expend one use of your Bardic Inspiration to deal an additional 2d6 psychic damage to that target. You can do so only once per round on your turn. The psychic damage increases when you reach certain levels: 3d6 at 5th level, 5d6 at 10th level, and 8d6 at 15th level.

6.name: Words of Terror
6.description: If you speak to a humanoid alone for at least 1 minute, you can attempt to seed paranoia in its mind. At the end of the conversation, the target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or be frightened of you or another creature of your choice. The target is frightened in this way for 1 hour, until it is attacked or damaged, or until it witnesses its allies being attacked or damaged. If the target succeeds on its saving throw, the target has no hint that you tried to frighten it.

14.name: Mantle of Whispers
14.description: When a humanoid dies within 30 feet of you, you can magically capture its shadow using your reaction. You retain this shadow until you use it or you finish a long rest. You can use the shadow as an action. When you do so, it vanishes, magically transforming into a disguise that appears on you. You now look like the dead person, but healthy and alive. This disguise lasts for 1 hour or until you end it as a bonus action.

14.name: Shadow Lore
14.description: As an action, you magically whisper a phrase that only one creature of your choice within 30 feet of you can hear. The target must make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. It automatically succeeds if it doesn't share a language with you or if it can't hear you. On a successful save, your whisper sounds like unintelligible mumbling and has no effect. On a failed save, the target is charmed by you for the next 8 hours or until you or your allies attack it, damage it, or force it to make a saving throw. It interprets the whispers as a description of its most mortifying secret.

subclasses.name: College of Eloquence
subclasses.description: Master orator whose words sway minds

3.name: Silver Tongue
3.description: You are a master at saying the right thing at the right time. When you make a Charisma (Persuasion) or Charisma (Deception) check, you can treat a d20 roll of 9 or lower as a 10.

3.name: Unsettling Words
3.description: You can spin words laced with magic that unsettle a creature and cause it to doubt itself. As a bonus action, you can expend one use of your Bardic Inspiration and choose one creature you can see within 60 feet of you. Roll the Bardic Inspiration die. The creature must subtract the number rolled from the next saving throw it makes before the start of your next turn.

6.name: Unfailing Inspiration
6.description: Your inspiring words are so persuasive that others feel driven to succeed. When a creature adds one of your Bardic Inspiration dice to its ability check, attack roll, or saving throw and the roll fails, the creature can keep the Bardic Inspiration die.

6.name: Universal Speech
6.description: You have gained the ability to make your speech intelligible to any creature. As an action, choose one or more creatures within 60 feet of you, up to a number equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of one creature). The chosen creatures can magically understand you, regardless of the language you speak, for 1 hour.

14.name: Infectious Inspiration
14.description: When you successfully inspire someone, the power of your eloquence can now spread to someone else. When a creature within 60 feet of you adds one of your Bardic Inspiration dice to its ability check, attack roll, or saving throw and the roll succeeds, you can use your reaction to encourage a different creature (other than yourself) that can hear you within 60 feet of you, giving it a Bardic Inspiration die without expending any of your Bardic Inspiration uses.

subclasses.name: College of Creation
subclasses.description: Channel the Song of Creation to manifest reality

3.name: Mote of Potential
3.description: When you give a creature a Bardic Inspiration die, you can utter a note from the Song of Creation to create a Tiny mote of potential, which orbits within 5 feet of that creature. The mote is intangible and invulnerable, and it lasts until the Bardic Inspiration die is lost. The mote looks like a musical note, a star, a flower, or another symbol of art or life that you choose. Ability Check: Roll the Bardic Inspiration die twice and use the higher roll. Attack Roll: The mote thunderously shatters and each creature of your choice within 5 feet must make a Constitution save or take thunder damage equal to the roll of the Bardic Inspiration die. Saving Throw: Roll the Bardic Inspiration die twice and use the higher roll.

3.name: Performance of Creation
3.description: As an action, you can channel the magic of the Song of Creation to create one nonmagical item of your choice in an unoccupied space within 10 feet of you. The item must appear on a surface or in a liquid that can support it. The gp value of the item can't be more than 20 times your bard level, and the item must be Medium or smaller. The item glimmers softly, and a creature can faintly hear music when touching it. The created item disappears after a number of hours equal to your proficiency bonus.

6.name: Animating Performance
6.description: As an action, you can animate one Large or smaller nonmagical item within 30 feet of you that isn't being worn or carried. The animate item uses the Dancing Item stat block. It is friendly to you and your companions and obeys your commands. It lasts for 1 hour, until it is reduced to 0 hit points, or until you die. You can have only one item animated by this feature at a time.

14.name: Creative Crescendo
14.description: When you use your Performance of Creation feature, you can create more than one item at once. The number of items equals your Charisma modifier (minimum of two items). If you create an item that would exceed that number, you choose which of the previously created items disappears. Only one of these items can be of the maximum size you can create; the rest must be Small or Tiny.

subclasses.name: College of Spirits
subclasses.description: Channel spirits through tales and séances

3.name: Guiding Whispers
3.description: You can reach out to spirits to guide you and others. You learn the Guidance cantrip, which doesn't count against the number of bard cantrips you know. For you, it has a range of 60 feet when you cast it.

3.name: Spiritual Focus
3.description: You can use a candle, crystal ball, skull, spirit board, or tarokka deck as a spellcasting focus for your bard spells. When you cast a bard spell that deals damage or restores hit points through the focus, roll a d6, and you gain a bonus to one damage or healing roll of the spell equal to the number rolled.

3.name: Tales from Beyond
3.description: You reach out to spirits who tell their tales through you. While you are holding your Spiritual Focus, you can use a bonus action to expend one use of your Bardic Inspiration and roll on the Spirit Tales table using your Bardic Inspiration die to determine the tale the spirits direct you to tell. You retain the tale in mind until you bestow the tale's effect or you finish a short or long rest.

6.name: Spirit Session
6.description: Spirits provide you with supernatural insights. You can conduct an hour-long ritual channeling spirits using your Spiritual Focus. You can conduct the ritual during a short or long rest, and it can be done at the same time. At the end of the ritual, you temporarily learn one spell of your choice from any class. The spell must be of a level equal to the number of creatures that conducted the ritual or less, and it must be of a level you can cast, and it must be in the school of divination or necromancy. The spell counts as a bard spell for you but doesn't count against the number of bard spells you know.

14.name: Mystical Connection
14.description: You now have the ability to nudge the spirits to a tale you want. Whenever you roll on the Spirit Tales table, you can roll the die twice and choose which of the two effects to bestow. If you roll the same number on both dice, you can ignore the number and choose any effect on the table.

subclasses.name: College of Mirrors
subclasses.description: Bards of the College of Mirrors use illusion magic to create duplicates of themselves, confusing enemies and performing impossible feats

3.name: Mirror Image Mastery
3.description: You learn the Mirror Image spell, which doesn't count against the number of bard spells you know. When you cast Mirror Image, you create four duplicates instead of three, and each duplicate has AC equal to 10 + your Dexterity modifier + your proficiency bonus.

3.name: Reflective Performance
3.description: When you use your Bardic Inspiration, you can create an illusory duplicate of the target that lasts until the start of your next turn. The duplicate appears in an unoccupied space within 5 feet of the target and can distract enemies. Attack rolls against the target have disadvantage while the duplicate exists.

6.name: Hall of Mirrors
6.description: As an action, you can expend a use of Bardic Inspiration to create an illusory zone of mirrors in a 20-foot cube centered on a point you can see within 60 feet. The area becomes difficult terrain for creatures other than you. Creatures in the area have disadvantage on attack rolls, and you have advantage on attack rolls against creatures in the area. The zone lasts for 1 minute or until you lose concentration (as if concentrating on a spell).

14.name: Perfect Reflection
14.description: When a creature you can see targets you with an attack, you can use your reaction to swap places with one of your Mirror Image duplicates. The attack targets the duplicate instead. Additionally, when your last Mirror Image duplicate is destroyed, you can use your reaction to cast Mirror Image without expending a spell slot. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

blood_hunter.name: Blood Hunter
blood_hunter.description: A hunter who turned forbidden blood magic against the monsters it was made to serve. You carve runes into your own flesh to hunt what others fear, and you pay for that power in blood — sometimes yours.
features: Hunter's Bane - You have advantage on Survival checks to track fey, fiends, and undead, and on Intelligence checks to recall information about them
Blood Maledict - You can channel your vital essence to curse enemies through hemocraft magic. You learn blood curses as you gain levels
Crimson Rite - You can imbue your weapon with elemental energy at the cost of your own vitality, dealing extra rite damage on each hit
Fighting Style - You adopt a particular style of fighting as your specialty
Extra Attack - You can attack twice whenever you take the Attack action
Brand of Castigation - You brand a creature with hemocraft magic, dealing psychic damage when it harms you
Dark Augmentation - Your speed increases by 10 feet and you gain a bonus to Strength, Dexterity, and Constitution saving throws equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of +1)
Brand of Tethering - Your brand prevents creatures from using the Dash action or teleporting
Sanguine Mastery - You can reroll your hemocraft die and regain Blood Maledict uses on critical hits

subclasses.name: Order of the Ghostslayer
subclasses.description: Ghostslayers seek to destroy undead wherever they lurk, channeling the power of their hemocraft to create radiant rites

3.name: Rite of the Dawn
3.description: Your Crimson Rite damage type becomes radiant. While active, your weapon sheds bright light in a 20-foot radius. You gain resistance to necrotic damage and deal an additional hemocraft die of damage against undead.

3.name: Curse Specialist
3.description: Your blood curses can affect any creature type, regardless of whether it has blood.

7.name: Aether Walk
7.description: At the start of your turn, you can magically step into the veil between the planes as long as you aren't incapacitated. You can move through creatures and objects as if they were difficult terrain, and can see and affect creatures and objects on the Ethereal Plane. You take 1d10 force damage if you end your turn inside an object. This lasts a number of rounds equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of 1 round); if you are inside an object when it ends, you are shunted to the nearest unoccupied space and take force damage equal to twice the number of feet you moved. You can use this feature once per short or long rest, twice at 15th level.

11.name: Brand of Sundering
11.description: When you hit a branded creature with a weapon for which you have an active Crimson Rite, you deal an additional hemocraft die of rite damage. The brand also prevents the creature from moving through creatures or objects.

15.name: Blood Curse of the Exorcist
15.description: You learn the Blood Curse of the Exorcist. You can end the charmed, frightened, or possessed condition on a creature. When amplified, the creature imposing the condition takes 3d6 psychic damage and must save or be stunned until the end of your next turn.

18.name: Rite Revival
18.description: When you are reduced to 0 hit points while you have an active Crimson Rite, you can end all your active rites to drop to 1 hit point instead. You can use this feature once per long rest.

subclasses.name: Order of the Lycan
subclasses.description: Lycans embrace a controlled form of lycanthropy, transforming into fearsome hybrid forms to tear apart their enemies

3.name: Heightened Senses
3.description: You gain advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on hearing or smell.

3.name: Hybrid Transformation
3.description: As a bonus action, you can transform into a hybrid lycanthropic form for up to 1 hour (once per short rest). While transformed: Feral Might gives advantage on Strength checks and saves and +1 to melee damage; Resilient Hide grants resistance to nonmagical bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage (except silver) and +1 AC without heavy armor; Predatory Strikes lets you apply Crimson Rite to unarmed strikes (1d6 base) and make a bonus unarmed strike; Bloodlust forces a DC 8 Wisdom save when below half HP or you must attack the nearest creature.

7.name: Stalker's Prowess
7.description: Your speed increases by 10 feet. Your long jump distance increases by 10 feet and high jump by 3 feet. Your unarmed strikes in hybrid form gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls.

11.name: Advanced Transformation
11.description: You can use Hybrid Transformation twice per short rest. While transformed and below half HP, you regenerate hit points equal to 1 + your Constitution modifier at the start of each turn. Your Feral Might melee damage bonus increases to +2.

15.name: Brand of the Voracious
15.description: You have advantage on Bloodlust saving throws. While in hybrid form, you have advantage on attack rolls against branded creatures.

18.name: Hybrid Transformation Mastery
18.description: You can use Hybrid Transformation an unlimited number of times per rest and the form lasts indefinitely. Your Feral Might melee damage bonus increases to +3. You learn the Blood Curse of the Howl: creatures within 30 feet must succeed on a Wisdom save or become frightened of you.

subclasses.name: Order of the Mutant
subclasses.description: Mutants use forbidden alchemy to create mutagenic formulas that grant them powerful—but dangerous—physical enhancements

3.name: Mutagencraft
3.description: You learn four mutagen formulas that you can create and consume as a bonus action. Each mutagen grants a benefit and imposes a drawback for 1 hour. Formulas include options like: Celerity (+DEX, -WIS), Potency (+STR, -DEX), Sagacity (+INT, -CHA), and others. You learn additional formulas at levels 7, 11, 15, and 18. You can create one mutagen per short rest.

7.name: Strange Metabolism
7.description: You are immune to the poisoned condition and poison damage. As a bonus action, you can ignore the negative effects of one active mutagen for 1 minute. You can use this feature once per long rest.

11.name: Brand of Axiom
11.description: Branded creatures cannot benefit from invisibility or illusion magic. If a branded creature is in an alternate form (such as from polymorph), it must succeed on a Wisdom save or revert to its true form and be stunned until the end of your next turn.

15.name: Blood Curse of Corrosion
15.description: You learn the Blood Curse of Corrosion. As a bonus action, you force a creature to make a Constitution save or become poisoned. When amplified, the target takes 4d6 necrotic damage when you inflict the curse, and again each time it fails its Constitution save to end the curse.

18.name: Exalted Mutation
18.description: As a bonus action, you can end one active mutagen and activate a different one you know without expending a use of Mutagencraft. You can use this a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once) per long rest.

subclasses.name: Order of the Profane Soul
subclasses.description: Profane Soul blood hunters forge pacts with lesser otherworldly beings, gaining warlock-like spellcasting alongside their hemocraft abilities

3.name: Otherworldly Patron
3.description: You forge a pact with an otherworldly being. Choose from The Archfey, The Celestial, The Fiend, or The Great Old One. Your patron grants you specific rite focus benefits when your Crimson Rite is active.

3.name: Pact Magic
3.description: You gain the ability to cast warlock spells using Intelligence as your spellcasting ability. You learn two cantrips and have pact magic spell slots that recharge on a short rest. Spell progression is slower than a full warlock, reaching 4th-level spells at most.

3.name: Rite Focus
3.description: While your Crimson Rite is active on a weapon, it serves as your spellcasting focus. Your patron grants a unique benefit: Archfey — a creature you damage with the rite weapon glows with faint light until the end of your next turn and gains no benefit from cover or being invisible; Celestial — as a bonus action, expend a use of Blood Maledict to heal a creature within 60 feet for one Hemocraft die plus your Intelligence modifier (minimum of +1); Fiend — while using the Rite of the Flame, reroll 1s and 2s on the rite damage dice; Great Old One — on a critical hit, the target and creatures of your choice within 10 feet of it are frightened until the end of your next turn.

7.name: Mystic Frenzy
7.description: When you use your action to cast a cantrip, you can make one weapon attack as a bonus action.

7.name: Revealed Arcana
7.description: Your patron grants you a spell you can cast once per long rest without expending a spell slot: Archfey — Blur; Celestial — Lesser Restoration; Fiend — Scorching Ray; Great Old One — Detect Thoughts.

11.name: Brand of the Sapping Scar
11.description: Branded creatures have disadvantage on saving throws against your warlock spells.

15.name: Unsealed Arcana
15.description: Your patron grants an additional spell you can cast once per long rest without expending a slot: Archfey — Slow; Celestial — Revivify; Fiend — Fireball; Great Old One — Haste.

18.name: Blood Curse of the Soul Eater
18.description: You learn the Blood Curse of the Soul Eater. When a creature within 30 feet drops to 0 HP, you gain advantage on attack rolls and resistance to all damage until the end of your next turn. When amplified, you also regain one expended warlock spell slot.

cleric.name: Cleric
cleric.description: You are your god's hand in the world — mending the wounded, turning back the dead, and calling down holy power when the fight turns desperate. Your domain shapes everything: a Life cleric heals, a War cleric leads the charge, a Trickery cleric is never where you think they are.
features: Spellcasting - You can cast cleric spells using Wisdom as your spellcasting ability
Cleric Subclass - Choose a domain related to your deity

subclasses.name: Life Domain
subclasses.description: Master of healing and preservation of life

1.name: Bonus Proficiency
1.description: You gain proficiency with heavy armor.

1.name: Disciple of Life
1.description: Your healing spells are more effective. Whenever you use a spell of 1st level or higher to restore hit points, the creature regains additional hit points equal to 2 + the spell's level.

2.name: Channel Divinity: Preserve Life
2.description: As an action, you present your holy symbol and evoke healing energy that restores a number of hit points equal to five times your cleric level. Choose any creatures within 30 feet, dividing those hit points among them (can't restore more than half their max HP).

6.name: Blessed Healer
6.description: When you cast a spell of 1st level or higher that restores hit points to a creature other than you, you regain hit points equal to 2 + the spell's level.

8.name: Divine Strike
8.description: Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can cause the attack to deal an extra 1d8 radiant damage. At 14th level, the extra damage increases to 2d8.

17.name: Supreme Healing
17.description: When you would normally roll one or more dice to restore hit points with a spell, you instead use the highest number possible for each die.

subclasses.name: War Domain
subclasses.description: Warrior priest who excels in battle

1.name: Bonus Proficiencies
1.description: You gain proficiency with martial weapons and heavy armor.

1.name: War Priest
1.description: When you use the Attack action, you can make one weapon attack as a bonus action. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum once), regaining all uses after a long rest.

2.name: Channel Divinity: Guided Strike
2.description: When you make an attack roll, you can use your Channel Divinity to gain a +10 bonus to the roll. You make this choice after you see the roll, but before the DM says whether the attack hits or misses.

6.name: Channel Divinity: War God's Blessing
6.description: When a creature within 30 feet makes an attack roll, you can use your reaction to grant that creature a +10 bonus to the roll, using your Channel Divinity.

8.name: Divine Strike
8.description: Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can cause the attack to deal an extra 1d8 damage of the same type dealt by the weapon. At 14th level, the extra damage increases to 2d8.

17.name: Avatar of Battle
17.description: You gain resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical attacks.

subclasses.name: Trickery Domain
subclasses.description: Master of illusion and deception

1.name: Blessing of the Trickster
1.description: You can use your action to touch a willing creature other than yourself to give it advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks. This blessing lasts for 1 hour or until you use this feature again.

2.name: Channel Divinity: Invoke Duplicity
2.description: As an action, you create a perfect illusion of yourself that lasts for 1 minute. You can cast spells as though you were in the illusion's space and gain advantage on attack rolls against creatures within 5 feet of both you and the illusion.

6.name: Channel Divinity: Cloak of Shadows
6.description: As an action, you become invisible until the end of your next turn. You become visible if you attack or cast a spell.

8.name: Divine Strike
8.description: Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can cause the attack to deal an extra 1d8 poison damage. At 14th level, the extra damage increases to 2d8.

17.name: Improved Duplicity
17.description: You can create up to four duplicates of yourself instead of one when you use Invoke Duplicity. You can move any number of them up to 30 feet as a bonus action.

subclasses.name: Knowledge Domain
subclasses.description: Scholar who collects and shares divine knowledge
bonusSkills: Choose two from: Arcana, History, Nature, Religion (expertise)

1.name: Blessings of Knowledge
1.description: You learn two languages of your choice. You also become proficient in two skills of your choice from: Arcana, History, Nature, or Religion. Your proficiency bonus is doubled for checks using either skill.

2.name: Channel Divinity: Knowledge of the Ages
2.description: As an action, you gain proficiency with one skill or tool of your choice for 10 minutes.

6.name: Channel Divinity: Read Thoughts
6.description: You can use your Channel Divinity to read a creature's thoughts. You can then use your access to the creature's mind to command it (as Suggestion spell).

8.name: Potent Spellcasting
8.description: You add your Wisdom modifier to the damage you deal with any cleric cantrip.

17.name: Visions of the Past
17.description: You can call up visions of the past. Object Reading or Area Reading for up to a number of minutes equal to your Wisdom score.

subclasses.name: Light Domain
subclasses.description: Bearer of divine radiance who banishes darkness

1.name: Bonus Cantrip
1.description: You gain the Light cantrip if you don't already know it.

1.name: Warding Flare
1.description: When you are attacked by a creature within 30 feet that you can see, you can use your reaction to impose disadvantage on the attack roll. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum once).

2.name: Channel Divinity: Radiance of the Dawn
2.description: As an action, you present your holy symbol and dispel magical darkness within 30 feet. Each hostile creature within 30 feet must make a Constitution saving throw, taking 2d10 + your cleric level radiant damage on a failed save, or half as much on a successful one.

6.name: Improved Flare
6.description: You can use your Warding Flare feature when a creature you can see within 30 feet attacks a creature other than you.

8.name: Potent Spellcasting
8.description: You add your Wisdom modifier to the damage you deal with any cleric cantrip.

17.name: Corona of Light
17.description: As an action, you activate an aura of sunlight that lasts for 1 minute. You emit bright light in a 60-foot radius and dim light 30 feet beyond that. Enemies in the bright light have disadvantage on saving throws against spells that deal fire or radiant damage.

subclasses.name: Nature Domain
subclasses.description: Servant of the gods of nature, flora, and fauna
bonusSkills: Choose one from: Animal Handling, Nature, Survival

1.name: Acolyte of Nature
1.description: You learn one druid cantrip of your choice. You also gain proficiency in one of the following skills: Animal Handling, Nature, or Survival.

1.name: Bonus Proficiency
1.description: You gain proficiency with heavy armor.

2.name: Channel Divinity: Charm Animals and Plants
2.description: As an action, you present your holy symbol and invoke the name of your deity. Each beast or plant creature that can see you within 30 feet must make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, the creature is charmed by you for 1 minute or until it takes damage.

6.name: Dampen Elements
6.description: When you or a creature within 30 feet takes acid, cold, fire, lightning, or thunder damage, you can use your reaction to grant resistance to that damage.

8.name: Divine Strike
8.description: Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can cause the attack to deal an extra 1d8 cold, fire, or lightning damage (your choice). At 14th level, the extra damage increases to 2d8.

17.name: Master of Nature
17.description: You gain the ability to command animals and plant creatures. While creatures are charmed by your Charm Animals and Plants feature, you can take a bonus action to verbally command what they do on their next turn.

subclasses.name: Tempest Domain
subclasses.description: Wrath of the storm, commanding thunder and lightning

1.name: Bonus Proficiencies
1.description: You gain proficiency with martial weapons and heavy armor.

1.name: Wrath of the Storm
1.description: When a creature within 5 feet of you that you can see hits you with an attack, you can use your reaction to cause the creature to make a Dexterity saving throw. The creature takes 2d8 lightning or thunder damage (your choice) on a failed save, or half as much on a successful one. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum once).

2.name: Channel Divinity: Destructive Wrath
2.description: When you roll lightning or thunder damage, you can use your Channel Divinity to deal maximum damage instead of rolling.

6.name: Thunderbolt Strike
6.description: When you deal lightning damage to a Large or smaller creature, you can also push it up to 10 feet away from you.

8.name: Divine Strike
8.description: Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can cause the attack to deal an extra 1d8 thunder damage. At 14th level, the extra damage increases to 2d8.

17.name: Stormborn
17.description: You have a flying speed equal to your current walking speed whenever you are not underground or indoors.

subclasses.name: Forge Domain
subclasses.description: Divine smith who creates magical items

1.name: Bonus Proficiencies
1.description: You gain proficiency with heavy armor and smith's tools.

1.name: Blessing of the Forge
1.description: At the end of a long rest, you can touch one nonmagical object that is a suit of armor or a simple or martial weapon. Until the end of your next long rest or until you die, the object becomes a magic item, granting a +1 bonus to AC (if armor) or attack and damage rolls (if weapon).

2.name: Channel Divinity: Artisan's Blessing
2.description: You conduct an hour-long ritual to craft a nonmagical item that must include some metal: a simple or martial weapon, a suit of armor, ten pieces of ammunition, a set of tools, or another metal object. At the end of the ritual, you create the item (worth up to 100 gp).

6.name: Soul of the Forge
6.description: You gain resistance to fire damage. While wearing heavy armor, you gain a +1 bonus to AC.

8.name: Divine Strike
8.description: Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can cause the attack to deal an extra 1d8 fire damage. At 14th level, the extra damage increases to 2d8.

17.name: Saint of Forge and Fire
17.description: You gain immunity to fire damage. While wearing heavy armor, you have resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical attacks.

subclasses.name: Grave Domain
subclasses.description: Guardian of the line between life and death

1.name: Circle of Mortality
1.description: When you would normally roll one or more dice to restore hit points with a spell to a creature at 0 hit points, you instead use the highest number possible for each die. In addition, you learn the Spare the Dying cantrip, which has a range of 30 feet for you.

1.name: Eyes of the Grave
1.description: As an action, you can magically sense the presence of undead within 60 feet that aren't behind total cover. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier.

2.name: Channel Divinity: Path to the Grave
2.description: As an action, you choose one creature you can see within 30 feet, cursing it until the end of your next turn. The next time you or an ally hits the cursed creature with an attack, the creature has vulnerability to all of that attack's damage.

6.name: Sentinel at Death's Door
6.description: As a reaction when you or a creature within 30 feet suffers a critical hit, you can turn that hit into a normal hit. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier.

8.name: Potent Spellcasting
8.description: You add your Wisdom modifier to the damage you deal with any cleric cantrip.

17.name: Keeper of Souls
17.description: When an enemy you can see dies within 60 feet of you, you or one creature of your choice within 60 feet regains hit points equal to the enemy's number of Hit Dice. You can use this feature only if you aren't incapacitated.

subclasses.name: Order Domain
subclasses.description: Voice of divine authority who commands obedience

1.name: Bonus Proficiencies
1.description: You gain proficiency with heavy armor. You also gain proficiency in the Intimidation or Persuasion skill (your choice).

1.name: Voice of Authority
1.description: If you cast a spell with a spell slot of 1st level or higher and target an ally, that ally can use their reaction immediately after the spell to make one weapon attack against a creature of your choice that you can see.

2.name: Channel Divinity: Order's Demand
2.description: As an action, you present your holy symbol and each creature of your choice that can see or hear you within 30 feet must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or be charmed by you until the end of your next turn or until it takes damage. You can also cause any charmed creatures to drop what they are holding.

6.name: Embodiment of the Law
6.description: If you cast a spell of the enchantment school using a spell slot of 1st level or higher, you can change the spell's casting time to 1 bonus action for this casting (if it's normally 1 action). You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier.

8.name: Divine Strike
8.description: Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can cause the attack to deal an extra 1d8 psychic damage. At 14th level, the extra damage increases to 2d8.

17.name: Order's Wrath
17.description: Enemies you deal Divine Strike damage to are cursed until the start of your next turn. The next time an ally hits the cursed creature with an attack, the target also takes 2d8 psychic damage, and the curse ends.

subclasses.name: Peace Domain
subclasses.description: Emissary of harmony who strengthens bonds

1.name: Implement of Peace
1.description: You gain proficiency in the Insight, Performance, or Persuasion skill (your choice).

1.name: Emboldening Bond
1.description: You can forge an empowering bond among people. As an action, choose a number of willing creatures within 30 feet equal to your proficiency bonus. For 10 minutes, when a bonded creature makes an attack roll, ability check, or saving throw, it can add a d4 to the roll (once per turn). You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus.

2.name: Channel Divinity: Balm of Peace
2.description: As an action, you move up to your speed without provoking opportunity attacks, and when you move within 5 feet of any other creature, you can restore a number of hit points to that creature equal to 2d6 + your Wisdom modifier. A creature can receive this healing only once.

6.name: Protective Bond
6.description: When a creature affected by your Emboldening Bond is about to take damage, a second bonded creature within 30 feet can use its reaction to teleport to an unoccupied space within 5 feet of the first creature and take all the damage instead.

8.name: Potent Spellcasting
8.description: You add your Wisdom modifier to the damage you deal with any cleric cantrip.

17.name: Expansive Bond
17.description: The benefits of your Emboldening Bond and Protective Bond features now work when the creatures are within 60 feet of each other. Moreover, when a creature uses Protective Bond to take someone else's damage, the creature has resistance to that damage.

subclasses.name: Twilight Domain
subclasses.description: Guardian who brings comfort and protection in darkness

1.name: Bonus Proficiencies
1.description: You gain proficiency with martial weapons and heavy armor.

1.name: Eyes of Night
1.description: You can see through the deepest gloom. You have darkvision out to a range of 300 feet. As an action, you can magically share this darkvision with willing creatures you can see within 10 feet (up to your Wisdom modifier). The shared darkvision lasts for 1 hour.

2.name: Channel Divinity: Twilight Sanctuary
2.description: As an action, you present your holy symbol and a sphere of twilight emanates from you (30-foot radius). It lasts for 1 minute, moving with you. At the end of each of your turns, each creature (including you) of your choice in the sphere gains temporary hit points equal to 1d6 + your cleric level, or ends one effect causing it to be charmed or frightened.

6.name: Steps of Night
6.description: You can draw on the mystical power of night to rise into the air. As a bonus action when you are in dim light or darkness, you can magically give yourself a flying speed equal to your walking speed for 1 minute. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus.

8.name: Divine Strike
8.description: Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can cause the attack to deal an extra 1d8 radiant damage. At 14th level, the extra damage increases to 2d8.

17.name: Twilight Shroud
17.description: The twilight that you summon offers a protective embrace: you and your allies have half cover while in the sphere created by your Twilight Sanctuary.

subclasses.name: Death Domain
subclasses.description: Dark priest who wields necrotic power

1.name: Bonus Proficiency
1.description: You gain proficiency with martial weapons.

1.name: Reaper
1.description: You learn one necromancy cantrip of your choice from any spell list. When you cast a necromancy cantrip that normally targets only one creature, the spell can instead target two creatures within range and within 5 feet of each other.

2.name: Channel Divinity: Touch of Death
2.description: When you hit a creature with a melee attack, you can use your Channel Divinity to deal extra necrotic damage equal to 5 + twice your cleric level.

6.name: Inescapable Destruction
6.description: Your ability to channel negative energy becomes more potent. Necrotic damage dealt by your cleric spells and Channel Divinity options ignores resistance to necrotic damage.

8.name: Divine Strike
8.description: Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can cause the attack to deal an extra 1d8 necrotic damage. At 14th level, the extra damage increases to 2d8.

17.name: Improved Reaper
17.description: When you cast a necromancy spell of 1st through 5th level that targets only one creature, the spell can instead target two creatures within range and within 5 feet of each other.

subclasses.name: Revelry Domain
subclasses.description: Clerics of the Revelry Domain serve deities of celebration, joy, wine, and festivity, spreading merriment and using the power of revelry to bolster allies and confound enemies

1.name: Bonus Proficiency
1.description: You gain proficiency in the Performance skill and with brewer's supplies.

1.name: Intoxicating Presence
1.description: Your divine connection to revelry allows you to spread joy. As an action, choose a creature within 30 feet. That creature must make a Wisdom saving throw or become charmed by you for 1 minute. While charmed in this way, the creature has disadvantage on Wisdom checks and its speed is reduced by 10 feet. The creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier.

2.name: Channel Divinity: Toast to Good Fortune
2.description: As an action, you raise a drink (or mime the gesture) and invoke your deity's blessing. Choose a number of creatures you can see within 30 feet equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum 1). Each creature gains temporary hit points equal to 2d6 + your cleric level and has advantage on their next attack roll or saving throw made within the next minute.

6.name: Spirit of the Party
6.description: You and allies within 10 feet of you are immune to the frightened condition while you are conscious. Additionally, when you or an ally within 10 feet fails a saving throw against being charmed, you can use your reaction to grant advantage on a reroll.

8.name: Potent Spellcasting
8.description: You add your Wisdom modifier to the damage you deal with any cleric cantrip.

17.name: Divine Bacchanal
17.description: As an action, you can create an area of divine revelry in a 30-foot radius centered on yourself that lasts for 1 minute. Allies in the area have advantage on saving throws against being charmed or frightened and regain 10 hit points at the start of their turns. Enemies in the area have disadvantage on attack rolls and must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw at the start of their turns or be incapacitated until the start of their next turn. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest.

subclasses.name: Wealth Domain
subclasses.description: Clerics of the Wealth Domain serve gods of commerce, treasure, and prosperity, using divine favor to enrich their allies and control the flow of fortune

1.name: Bonus Proficiency
1.description: You gain proficiency in Persuasion or Deception (your choice), and with one of the following: land vehicles, water vehicles, navigator's tools, or jeweler's tools.

1.name: Eye for Value
1.description: Your divine connection to wealth grants you supernatural appraisal abilities. You double your proficiency bonus on any ability check you make to determine the monetary value of objects, gems, art, or trade goods. You can also sense the approximate value of treasure within 30 feet as an action.

2.name: Channel Divinity: Golden Favor
2.description: As an action, you present your holy symbol and conjure a shimmering pile of coins and gems worth up to 50 gp × your cleric level. This treasure is real but temporary — it reverts to worthless lead after 1 hour. While it exists, it can be used for bribes, trade, or as material components for spells.

6.name: Merchant's Blessing
6.description: Your deity's favor extends to commerce. You and your allies purchase goods and services at a 25% discount in settlements where your deity is known. Additionally, once per long rest when an ally within 30 feet makes an ability check, you can spend gold pieces equal to 10 × your cleric level to grant that ally a bonus to the roll equal to your Wisdom modifier.

8.name: Potent Spellcasting
8.description: You add your Wisdom modifier to the damage you deal with any cleric cantrip.

17.name: Fortune's Chosen
17.description: Once per 7 days, you can spend 1 hour in prayer and sacrifice 1,000 gp worth of offerings to petition your deity for aid. The deity grants one of the following: a rare magic item (temporary, lasts 7 days), the answer to a single question (as the Commune spell but with greater detail), or a blessing of prosperity (you and up to 6 allies gain advantage on all ability checks and saving throws for 24 hours).

subclasses.name: Stone Domain
subclasses.description: Clerics of the Stone Domain draw power from the enduring earth, wielding the strength of mountains and the patience of stone to protect their allies

1.name: Bonus Proficiency
1.description: You gain proficiency with heavy armor and mason's tools.

1.name: Stone's Endurance
1.description: When you take damage, you can use your reaction to encase yourself briefly in protective stone, gaining resistance to all damage except psychic until the start of your next turn. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum 1), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

2.name: Channel Divinity: Stoneward Shield
2.description: As an action, you call upon the strength of the earth to protect yourself or an ally within 30 feet.
