The target gains temporary hit points equal to your cleric level + your Wisdom modifier and a bonus to AC equal to your Wisdom modifier. This effect lasts for 1 minute or until the temporary hit points are depleted.

6.name: Earthen Rebuke
6.description: When you or an ally within 5 feet takes damage from a melee attack, you can use your reaction to reduce the damage by 1d8 + your Wisdom modifier as stone momentarily encases the target. The stone then shatters outward — the attacker must make a Dexterity saving throw or take 1d8 + your Wisdom modifier piercing damage. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier per long rest.

8.name: Divine Strike
8.description: Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can cause the attack to deal an extra 1d8 bludgeoning damage. When you reach 14th level, the extra damage increases to 2d8.

17.name: Heart of the Mountain
17.description: You gain a burrow speed equal to your walking speed and can move through nonmagical unworked stone or metal as if it were difficult terrain without disturbing it. While underground, you have tremorsense out to 60 feet. Additionally, you have resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical weapons.

druid.name: Druid
druid.description: A priest of the Old Faith, bound to the wild — forests, storms, beasts, and the turning of seasons. You wear animal shapes as easily as your own skin, and call down the fury of nature on anything that threatens the wild.
features: Spellcasting - You can cast druid spells using Wisdom as your spellcasting ability
Druidic - You know Druidic, the secret language of druids
Wild Shape - You can magically assume the shape of a beast

subclasses.name: Circle of the Land
subclasses.description: Mystic whose power comes from the land itself

2.name: Bonus Cantrip
2.description: You learn one additional druid cantrip of your choice.

2.name: Natural Recovery
2.description: During a short rest, you can recover expended spell slots. The spell slots can have a combined level that is equal to or less than half your druid level (rounded up), and none of the slots can be 6th level or higher. You can't use this feature again until you finish a long rest.

3.name: Circle Spells
3.description: Your mystical connection to the land infuses you with the ability to cast certain spells. You gain access to circle spells connected to the land where you became a druid. These spells are always prepared and don't count against your prepared spells.

6.name: Land's Stride
6.description: Moving through nonmagical difficult terrain costs you no extra movement. You can also pass through nonmagical plants without being slowed by them and without taking damage from them if they have thorns, spines, or a similar hazard. You have advantage on saving throws against plants that are magically created or manipulated to impede movement.

10.name: Nature's Ward
10.description: You can't be charmed or frightened by elementals or fey, and you are immune to poison and disease.

14.name: Nature's Sanctuary
14.description: Creatures of the natural world sense your connection to nature and become hesitant to attack you. When a beast or plant creature attacks you, that creature must make a Wisdom saving throw against your druid spell save DC. On a failed save, the creature must choose a different target, or the attack automatically misses.

subclasses.name: Circle of the Moon
subclasses.description: Fierce guardian who can transform into powerful beasts

2.name: Combat Wild Shape
2.description: You can use Wild Shape as a bonus action, rather than as an action. Additionally, while you are transformed by Wild Shape, you can use a bonus action to expend one spell slot to regain 1d8 hit points per level of the spell slot expended.

2.name: Circle Forms
2.description: You can transform into a beast with a challenge rating as high as 1 (ignoring the Max. CR column of the Beast Shapes table). Starting at 6th level, you can transform into a beast with a challenge rating as high as your druid level divided by 3, rounded down.

6.name: Primal Strike
6.description: Your attacks in beast form count as magical for the purpose of overcoming resistance and immunity to nonmagical attacks and damage.

10.name: Elemental Wild Shape
10.description: You can expend two uses of Wild Shape at the same time to transform into an air elemental, an earth elemental, a fire elemental, or a water elemental.

14.name: Thousand Forms
14.description: You have learned to use magic to alter your physical form in more subtle ways. You can cast the Alter Self spell at will.

subclasses.name: Circle of Dreams
subclasses.description: Guardian of the dreaming world with ties to the Feywild

2.name: Balm of the Summer Court
2.description: You have a pool of fey energy represented by a number of d6s equal to your druid level. As a bonus action, you can choose a creature you can see within 120 feet and spend a number of those dice equal to half your druid level or less. Roll the spent dice and add them together. The target regains a number of hit points equal to the total. The target also gains 1 temporary hit point per die spent. You regain all expended dice when you finish a long rest.

6.name: Hearth of Moonlight and Shadow
6.description: At the start of a rest, you can create a 30-foot-radius sphere of magic in an area. Within the sphere, you and your allies gain a +5 bonus to Dexterity (Stealth) and Wisdom (Perception) checks, and any light from open flames in the sphere (a campfire, torches, or the like) isn't visible outside it. The sphere vanishes at the end of the rest or when you leave the sphere.

10.name: Hidden Paths
10.description: You can use the hidden, magical pathways that some fey use to traverse space in the blink of an eye. As a bonus action, you can teleport up to 60 feet to an unoccupied space you can see. Alternatively, you can use your action to teleport one willing creature you touch up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space you can see. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of once).

14.name: Walker in Dreams
14.description: The magic of the Feywild grants you the ability to travel mentally or physically through dreamlands. When you finish a short rest, you can cast one of the following spells, without expending a spell slot or requiring material components: Dream (with you as the messenger), Scrying, or Teleportation Circle. This use of Teleportation Circle is special. Rather than opening a portal to a permanent teleportation circle, it opens a portal to the last location where you finished a long rest on your current plane of existence.

subclasses.name: Circle of the Shepherd
subclasses.description: Protector of nature's creatures and summoner of spirits

2.name: Speech of the Woods
2.description: You gain the ability to converse with beasts and many fey. You learn to speak, read, and write Sylvan. In addition, beasts can understand your speech, and you gain the ability to decipher their noises and motions.

2.name: Spirit Totem
2.description: As a bonus action, you can magically summon an incorporeal spirit to a point you can see within 60 feet of you. The spirit creates an aura in a 30-foot radius around that point. It counts as neither a creature nor an object, though it has the spectral appearance of the creature it represents. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus. Choose Bear Spirit (temp HP, advantage on Strength checks), Hawk Spirit (advantage on Perception, advantage on attack rolls), or Unicorn Spirit (advantage on detecting creatures, healing bonus when you cast healing spells).

6.name: Mighty Summoner
6.description: Beasts and fey that you conjure are more resilient than normal. Any beast or fey summoned or created by a spell that you cast gains the following benefits: the creature appears with more hit points than normal: 2 extra hit points per Hit Die it has, and the damage from its natural weapons is considered magical.

10.name: Guardian Spirit
10.description: Your Spirit Totem safeguards the beasts and fey that you call forth with your magic. When a beast or fey that you summoned or created with a spell ends its turn in your Spirit Totem aura, that creature regains a number of hit points equal to half your druid level.

14.name: Faithful Summons
14.description: The nature spirits you commune with protect you when you are the most defenseless. If you are reduced to 0 hit points or are incapacitated against your will, you can immediately gain the benefits of Conjure Animals as if it were cast using a 9th-level spell slot. It summons four beasts of your choice that are challenge rating 2 or lower. The conjured beasts appear within 20 feet of you.

subclasses.name: Circle of Spores
subclasses.description: Druid who draws power from decay and fungal growth

2.name: Halo of Spores
2.description: You are surrounded by invisible, necrotic spores that are harmless until you unleash them on a creature nearby. When a creature you can see moves into a space within 10 feet of you or starts its turn there, you can use your reaction to deal 1d4 necrotic damage to that creature unless it succeeds on a Constitution saving throw. The necrotic damage increases to 1d6 at 6th level, 1d8 at 10th level, and 1d10 at 14th level.

2.name: Symbiotic Entity
2.description: You can use your Wild Shape to awaken spores that infuse you with power for 10 minutes. You gain 4 temporary hit points for each level you have in this class. While this feature is active, you gain the following benefits: When you deal your Halo of Spores damage, roll the damage die a second time and add it to the total. Your melee weapon attacks deal an extra 1d6 necrotic damage to any target they hit.

6.name: Fungal Infestation
6.description: Your spores gain the ability to infest a corpse and animate it. If a beast or a humanoid that is Small or Medium dies within 10 feet of you, you can use your reaction to animate it, causing it to stand up immediately with 1 hit point. The creature uses the zombie stat block. It remains animate for 1 hour, after which time it collapses and dies. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier.

10.name: Spreading Spores
10.description: You gain the ability to seed an area with deadly spores. As a bonus action while your Symbiotic Entity feature is active, you can hurl spores up to 30 feet away, where they swirl in a 10-foot cube for 1 minute. The spores disappear early if you use this feature again, if you dismiss them as a bonus action, or if your Symbiotic Entity feature is no longer active. Whenever a creature moves into the cube or starts its turn there, that creature takes your Halo of Spores damage.

14.name: Fungal Body
14.description: The fungal spores in your body alter you: you can't be blinded, deafened, frightened, or poisoned, and any critical hit against you counts as a normal hit instead, unless you're incapacitated.

subclasses.name: Circle of Stars
subclasses.description: Druid who draws power from starlight and constellations

2.name: Star Map
2.description: You've created a star chart as part of your study. While holding this map, you have these benefits: You know the Guidance cantrip. You have the Guiding Bolt spell prepared (doesn't count against your prepared spells and you can cast it without expending a spell slot a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus).

2.name: Starry Form
2.description: As a bonus action, you can expend a use of Wild Shape to take on a starry form for 10 minutes. You shed bright light in a 10-foot radius and dim light for an additional 10 feet. Choose Archer (bonus action ranged spell attack dealing radiant damage), Chalice (when you cast a healing spell, you or another creature within 30 feet regains hit points), or Dragon (treat any roll of 9 or lower on Intelligence or Wisdom checks or Constitution saves to maintain concentration as a 10).

6.name: Cosmic Omen
6.description: You learn to use your star map to divine the will of the cosmos. Whenever you finish a long rest, you can consult your Star Map for omens. When you do so, roll a die. Until you finish your next long rest, you can use a reaction to add or subtract the number rolled to a creature's attack roll, saving throw, or ability check (Weal or Woe based on roll).

10.name: Twinkling Constellations
10.description: The constellations of your Starry Form improve. The 1d8 of the Archer and the Chalice becomes 2d8, and while the Dragon is active, you also have a flying speed of 20 feet and can hover. Moreover, at the start of each of your turns while in your Starry Form, you can change which constellation glimmers on your body.

14.name: Full of Stars
14.description: While in your Starry Form, you become partially incorporeal, giving you resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage.

subclasses.name: Circle of Wildfire
subclasses.description: Druid who understands fire's role in nature's cycle

2.name: Summon Wildfire Spirit
2.description: You can summon the primal spirit bound to your soul. As an action, you can expend one use of your Wild Shape feature to summon your wildfire spirit, rather than assuming a beast form. The spirit appears in an unoccupied space of your choice that you can see within 30 feet. Each creature within 10 feet of the spirit (other than you) when it appears must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or take 2d6 fire damage.

6.name: Enhanced Bond
6.description: The bond with your wildfire spirit enhances your destructive and restorative spells. Whenever you cast a spell that deals fire damage or restores hit points while your wildfire spirit is summoned, roll a d8, and you gain a bonus equal to the number rolled to one damage or healing roll of the spell. In addition, when you cast a spell with a range other than self, the spell can originate from you or your wildfire spirit.

10.name: Cauterizing Flames
10.description: When a Small or larger creature dies within 30 feet of you or your wildfire spirit, a harmless spectral flame springs forth in the dead creature's space and flickers there for 1 minute. When a creature you can see enters that space, you can use your reaction to extinguish the spectral flame there and either heal the creature or deal fire damage to it. You can use this reaction a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus.

14.name: Blazing Revival
14.description: The bond with your wildfire spirit can save you from death. If the spirit is within 120 feet of you when you are reduced to 0 hit points and thereby fall unconscious, you can cause the spirit to drop to 0 hit points. You then regain half your hit points and immediately rise to your feet. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest.

subclasses.name: Circle of Sand
subclasses.description: Druids of the Circle of Sand draw their power from the harsh beauty of deserts, commanding sand, wind, and the scorching sun to protect the natural world

2.name: Sand Shape
2.description: You can expend a use of Wild Shape to transform into a swirling elemental of sand rather than a beast. While in this form, you have resistance to nonmagical bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage, you can move through spaces as narrow as 1 inch without squeezing, and you have a burrow speed equal to your walking speed. You can use your action to create a 10-foot radius cloud of sand around yourself that lightly obscures the area until the start of your next turn.

6.name: Desert's Embrace
6.description: You gain resistance to fire damage. Additionally, you and creatures of your choice within 10 feet of you ignore difficult terrain caused by sand, dust, or loose earth. You also don't suffer the effects of extreme heat.

10.name: Sandstorm
10.description: As an action, you can create a sandstorm in a 30-foot radius centered on yourself that lasts for 1 minute or until you dismiss it (no action required). The area is heavily obscured for creatures other than you. Each creature other than you that starts its turn in the area or enters it for the first time on a turn must make a Constitution saving throw, taking 3d6 slashing damage on a failed save, or half as much on a successful one. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest.

14.name: One with the Desert
14.description: While in your Sand Shape form, you gain immunity to fire damage and the blinded condition. You can also cast spells while in Sand Shape without needing material components. Additionally, when you use your Sandstorm feature, you can choose a number of creatures equal to your Wisdom modifier to be unaffected by it.

fighter.name: Fighter
fighter.description: A master of arms who wins fights through skill, discipline, and sheer stubbornness. No tricks, no bargains — just the best-trained sword, bow, or shield on the field, and the grit to keep standing when everyone else falls.
features: Fighting Style - Choose a fighting style that grants combat bonuses
Second Wind - Regain Hit Points as a Bonus Action (2 uses; 3 at 4th, 4 at 10th)

subclasses.name: Champion
subclasses.description: Master of physical combat, excelling in critical hits

3.name: Improved Critical
3.description: Your weapon attacks score a critical hit on a roll of 19 or 20.

7.name: Remarkable Athlete
7.description: You can add half your proficiency bonus (round up) to any Strength, Dexterity, or Constitution check you make that doesn't already use your proficiency bonus. In addition, when you make a running long jump, the distance you can cover increases by a number of feet equal to your Strength modifier.

10.name: Additional Fighting Style
10.description: You can choose a second option from the Fighting Style class feature.

15.name: Superior Critical
15.description: Your weapon attacks score a critical hit on a roll of 18-20.

18.name: Survivor
18.description: You attain the pinnacle of resilience in battle. At the start of each of your turns, you regain hit points equal to 5 + your Constitution modifier if you have no more than half of your hit points left. You don't gain this benefit if you have 0 hit points.

subclasses.name: Battle Master
subclasses.description: Tactical warrior who uses maneuvers in combat

3.name: Combat Superiority
3.description: You learn maneuvers that are fueled by special dice called superiority dice. You learn three maneuvers of your choice. You have four superiority dice, which are d8s. A superiority die is expended when you use it. You regain all of your expended superiority dice when you finish a short or long rest. At 7th level you learn two additional maneuvers and gain another superiority die, and at 15th level you learn two more and gain another die.

3.name: Student of War
3.description: You gain proficiency with one type of artisan's tools of your choice.

7.name: Know Your Enemy
7.description: If you spend at least 1 minute observing or interacting with another creature outside combat, you can learn certain information about its capabilities compared to your own: Strength score, Dexterity score, Constitution score, Armor Class, Current hit points, Total class levels (if any), and Fighter class levels (if any).

10.name: Improved Combat Superiority
10.description: Your superiority dice turn into d10s.

15.name: Relentless
15.description: When you roll initiative and have no superiority dice remaining, you regain one superiority die.

18.name: Superior Combat Superiority
18.description: Your superiority dice turn into d12s.

subclasses.name: Eldritch Knight
subclasses.description: Fighter who supplements martial prowess with magic

3.name: Spellcasting
3.description: You learn to cast spells. You learn two cantrips of your choice from the wizard spell list. You learn three 1st-level wizard spells of your choice, two of which must be abjuration or evocation spells. Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for these spells.

3.name: War Bond
3.description: You learn a ritual that creates a magical bond between yourself and one weapon. Once you have bonded a weapon to yourself, you can't be disarmed of that weapon unless you are incapacitated. If it is on the same plane of existence, you can summon that weapon as a bonus action on your turn, causing it to teleport instantly to your hand.

7.name: War Magic
7.description: When you use your action to cast a cantrip, you can make one weapon attack as a bonus action.

10.name: Eldritch Strike
10.description: When you hit a creature with a weapon attack, that creature has disadvantage on the next saving throw it makes against a spell you cast before the end of your next turn.

15.name: Arcane Charge
15.description: When you use Action Surge, you can teleport up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space you can see. You can teleport before or after the additional action.

18.name: Improved War Magic
18.description: When you use your action to cast a spell, you can make one weapon attack as a bonus action.

subclasses.name: Cavalier
subclasses.description: Mounted warrior who excels at protecting allies

3.name: Bonus Proficiency
3.description: You gain proficiency in one of the following skills of your choice: Animal Handling, History, Insight, Performance, or Persuasion. Alternatively, you learn one language of your choice.

3.name: Born to the Saddle
3.description: Mounting or dismounting a creature costs you only 5 feet of movement. In addition, you have advantage on saving throws made to avoid falling off your mount. If you fall off your mount and descend no more than 10 feet, you can land on your feet if you're not incapacitated.

3.name: Unwavering Mark
3.description: When you hit a creature with a melee weapon attack, you can mark the creature until the end of your next turn. A marked creature has disadvantage on any attack roll that doesn't target you. If a creature marked by you deals damage to anyone other than you, you can make a special melee weapon attack against the marked creature as a bonus action on your next turn.

7.name: Warding Maneuver
7.description: You can use your reaction to make a creature within 5 feet of you that is hit by an attack have the attack deal half damage. If the attack would have reduced the creature to 0 hit points, it instead remains at 1 hit point. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Constitution modifier.

10.name: Hold the Line
10.description: Creatures provoke an opportunity attack from you when they move 5 feet or more while within your reach, and if you hit a creature with an opportunity attack, the target's speed is reduced to 0 until the end of the current turn.

15.name: Ferocious Charger
15.description: If you move at least 10 feet in a straight line right before attacking a creature and you hit it with the attack, that target must succeed on a Strength saving throw (DC 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Strength modifier) or be knocked prone.

18.name: Vigilant Defender
18.description: You respond to danger with extraordinary vigilance. In combat, you get a special reaction that you can take once on every creature's turn, except your turn. You can use this special reaction only to make an opportunity attack, and you can't use it on the same turn that you take your normal reaction.

subclasses.name: Samurai
subclasses.description: Warrior with iron will and devastating precision

3.name: Bonus Proficiency
3.description: You gain proficiency in one of the following skills of your choice: History, Insight, Performance, or Persuasion. Alternatively, you learn one language of your choice.

3.name: Fighting Spirit
3.description: Your intensity in battle can shield you and help you strike true. As a bonus action on your turn, you can give yourself advantage on weapon attack rolls until the end of the current turn. When you do so, you also gain 5 temporary hit points. The temporary hit points increase when you reach certain levels: 10 at 10th level and 15 at 15th level. You can use this feature three times.

7.name: Elegant Courtier
7.description: Your discipline and attention to detail allow you to excel in social situations. Whenever you make a Charisma (Persuasion) check, you gain a bonus to the check equal to your Wisdom modifier. You also gain proficiency in Wisdom saving throws. If you already have this proficiency, you instead gain proficiency in Intelligence or Charisma saving throws.

10.name: Tireless Spirit
10.description: When you roll initiative and have no uses of Fighting Spirit remaining, you regain one use.

15.name: Rapid Strike
15.description: You learn to trade accuracy for swift strikes. If you take the Attack action on your turn and have advantage on an attack roll against one of the targets, you can forgo the advantage for that roll to make an additional weapon attack against that target, as part of the same action. You can do so no more than once per turn.

18.name: Strength Before Death
18.description: If you take damage that reduces you to 0 hit points and doesn't kill you outright, you can use your reaction to delay falling unconscious, and you can immediately take an extra turn, interrupting the current turn. While you have 0 hit points during that extra turn, taking damage causes death saving throw failures as normal. Once the extra turn ends, you fall unconscious if you still have 0 hit points.

subclasses.name: Echo Knight
subclasses.description: Manifest echoes of yourself from alternate timelines

3.name: Manifest Echo
3.description: You can use a bonus action to magically manifest an echo of yourself in an unoccupied space you can see within 15 feet of you. This echo is a magical, translucent, gray image of you that lasts until it is destroyed, until you dismiss it as a bonus action, until you manifest another echo, or until you're incapacitated. Your echo has AC = 14 + your proficiency bonus, 1 hit point, and immunity to all conditions. When you take the Attack action on your turn, any attack you make with that action can originate from your space or the echo's space.

3.name: Unleash Incarnation
3.description: You can heighten your echo's fury. Whenever you take the Attack action, you can make one additional melee attack from the echo's position. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Constitution modifier.

7.name: Echo Avatar
7.description: You can temporarily transfer your consciousness to your echo. As an action, you can see through your echo's eyes and hear through its ears. During this time, you are deafened and blinded. You can sustain this effect for up to 10 minutes, and you can end it at any time. While your echo is being used in this way, it can be up to 1,000 feet away from you without being destroyed.

10.name: Shadow Martyr
10.description: You can make your echo throw itself in front of an attack directed at another creature that you can see. Before the attack roll is made, you can use your reaction to teleport the echo to an unoccupied space within 5 feet of the targeted creature. The attack roll that triggered the reaction is instead made against your echo.

15.name: Reclaim Potential
15.description: You've learned to absorb the fleeting magic of your echo. When an echo of yours is destroyed by taking damage, you can gain a number of temporary hit points equal to 2d6 + your Constitution modifier, provided you don't already have temporary hit points. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Constitution modifier.

18.name: Legion of One
18.description: You can use a bonus action to create two echoes with your Manifest Echo feature, and these echoes can coexist. If you try to create a third echo, the previous two echoes are destroyed. Anything you can do from one echo's position can be done from the other's instead. In addition, when you roll initiative and have no uses of Unleash Incarnation remaining, you regain one use.

subclasses.name: Rune Knight
subclasses.description: Channel the power of giant runes

3.name: Bonus Proficiencies
3.description: You gain proficiency with smith's tools, and you learn to speak, read, and write Giant.

3.name: Rune Carver
3.description: You can use magic runes to enhance your gear. You learn two runes of your choice, from among the runes described below. You can inscribe each rune you know onto one object. Whenever you finish a long rest, you can touch a number of objects equal to the number of runes you know, and you inscribe a different rune onto each of the objects.

3.name: Giant's Might
3.description: You have learned how to imbue yourself with the might of giants. As a bonus action, you magically gain the following benefits for 1 minute: If you are smaller than Large, you become Large, along with anything you are wearing. You have advantage on Strength checks and Strength saving throws. Once on each of your turns, one of your attacks with a weapon or an unarmed strike can deal an extra 1d6 damage to a target on a hit.

7.name: Runic Shield
7.description: You learn to invoke your rune magic to protect your allies. When another creature you can see within 60 feet of you is hit by an attack roll, you can use your reaction to force the attacker to reroll the d20 and use the new roll. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus.

10.name: Great Stature
10.description: The magic of your runes permanently alters you. When you gain this feature, roll 3d4. You grow a number of inches in height equal to the roll. Moreover, the extra damage you deal with your Giant's Might feature increases to 1d8.

15.name: Master of Runes
15.description: You can invoke each rune you know from your Rune Carver feature twice, rather than once, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a short or long rest.

18.name: Runic Juggernaut
18.description: You learn how to amplify your rune-powered transformation. As a result, the extra damage you deal with the Giant's Might feature increases to 1d10. Moreover, when you use that feature, your size can increase to Huge, and while you are that size, your reach increases by 5 feet.

subclasses.name: Psi Warrior
subclasses.description: Awaken psionic powers to augment combat abilities

3.name: Psionic Power
3.description: You harbor a wellspring of psionic energy within yourself. This energy is represented by your Psionic Energy dice, which are each a d6. You have a number of these dice equal to twice your proficiency bonus. You can use them for: Protective Field (reduce damage to yourself or allies), Psionic Strike (add force damage to attacks), or Telekinetic Movement (move objects or creatures).

3.name: Protective Field
3.description: When you or another creature you can see within 30 feet of you takes damage, you can use your reaction to expend one Psionic Energy die, roll the die, and reduce the damage taken by the number rolled plus your Intelligence modifier (minimum reduction of 1).

7.name: Telekinetic Adept
7.description: You have mastered new ways to use your telekinetic abilities. You can cast Telekinesis, requiring no components, and your spellcasting ability for the spell is Intelligence. You can also propel weapons telekinetically: when you hit with a weapon attack, you can push the target 10 feet away or toward you.

10.name: Guarded Mind
10.description: The psionic energy flowing through you has bolstered your mind. You have resistance to psychic damage. Moreover, if you start your turn charmed or frightened, you can expend a Psionic Energy die and end every effect on yourself subjecting you to those conditions.

15.name: Bulwark of Force
15.description: You can shield yourself and others with telekinetic force. As a bonus action, you can choose creatures, which can include you, that you can see within 30 feet of you, up to a number of creatures equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of one creature). Each of the chosen creatures is protected by half cover for 1 minute or until you're incapacitated.

18.name: Telekinetic Master
18.description: Your ability to move creatures and objects with your mind is matched by few. You can cast the Telekinesis spell, requiring no components, and your spellcasting ability for the spell is Intelligence. On each of your turns while you concentrate on the spell, including the turn when you cast it, you can make one attack with a weapon as a bonus action.

subclasses.name: Monster Hunter
subclasses.description: Fighters who dedicate themselves to hunting dangerous monsters, learning their weaknesses and developing specialized techniques to bring them down

3.name: Hunter's Knowledge
3.description: You gain proficiency in the Survival skill if you don't already have it. Your proficiency bonus is doubled for any ability check you make that uses Survival. Additionally, you learn to identify monsters. As an action, you can study a creature you can see within 60 feet. You learn its creature type, any damage resistances, immunities, or vulnerabilities it has, and any special abilities it has that you could observe.

3.name: Monster Slayer
3.description: You can mark a creature you can see as your quarry as a bonus action. For the next hour, you deal an extra 1d6 damage to the marked creature whenever you hit it with a weapon attack. This damage increases to 2d6 at 10th level and 3d6 at 18th level. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus.

7.name: Exploit Weakness
7.description: When you hit a creature marked by your Monster Slayer feature with a weapon attack, you can force it to make a Constitution saving throw (DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Strength or Dexterity modifier). On a failed save, the creature has disadvantage on attack rolls and ability checks until the end of your next turn.

10.name: Steel Nerves
10.description: You have advantage on saving throws against being frightened. Additionally, you can't be surprised by creatures of a type you've studied using your Hunter's Knowledge feature.

15.name: Slayer's Instinct
15.description: When a creature marked by your Monster Slayer feature hits you with an attack, you can use your reaction to make a weapon attack against that creature. Additionally, when you reduce a marked creature to 0 hit points, you regain one use of your Monster Slayer feature.

18.name: Legendary Hunter
18.description: You've become a legend among monster hunters. When you use your Monster Slayer feature, you can mark up to two creatures at once. When you use your Exploit Weakness feature and the creature fails its save, it is also stunned until the end of your next turn. Once a creature is stunned by this feature, it can't be stunned by it again for 24 hours.

subclasses.name: Spellwarden
subclasses.description: Anti-magic specialists who protect their allies from arcane threats, combining martial prowess with the ability to disrupt and counter spellcasters

3.name: Spellbreaker's Training
3.description: You gain proficiency in the Arcana skill. If you already have this proficiency, you gain proficiency in Investigation or Insight instead. You learn two cantrips of your choice from the wizard spell list. Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for these cantrips.

3.name: Arcane Shield
3.description: As a bonus action, you can conjure a shimmering arcane barrier around yourself. You gain temporary hit points equal to your Intelligence modifier + half your fighter level (minimum 1). While you have these temporary hit points, you have advantage on saving throws against spells and magical effects. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus per long rest.

7.name: Magister Knight
7.description: When you use your action to cast a cantrip, you can make one weapon attack as a bonus action. Additionally, when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can force it to make a Constitution saving throw (DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Intelligence modifier). On a failure, the creature has disadvantage on the next spell it casts before the end of its next turn.

10.name: Magister Defender
10.description: Friendly creatures within 10 feet of you can reroll a failed saving throw against a spell or magical effect, using the new roll. A creature can benefit from this feature only once per spell. Additionally, you gain resistance to damage from spells.

15.name: Indomitable Will
15.description: You gain proficiency in Wisdom saving throws. If you already have this proficiency, you gain proficiency in Charisma saving throws instead. Additionally, you are immune to the charmed condition.

18.name: Arcane Surge
18.description: When you use your Action Surge feature, you can also cast one 1st-level abjuration or evocation spell as part of the same turn without expending a spell slot. Your weapon attacks deal an additional 1d8 force damage for the rest of the turn. Additionally, when you hit a creature that is concentrating on a spell, it has disadvantage on the Constitution saving throw to maintain concentration.

keeper.name: Keeper
keeper.description: A scholar who draws power from literature, language, and myth. You pull weapons and wonders out of the stories you've studied, and speak passages of power that reshape the fight around you.
features: Recitation - Short verbal invocations (cantrip equivalent). Deal 1d8 psychic/force damage, grant temp HP, or force a WIS save. Scales at L5/11/17
Manifest Weapon - Bonus action: summon a weapon from a text you know. Uses CHA for attack and damage. Counts as magical. Lasts 1 minute or until dismissed
Keeper's Library - You know texts that each grant a weapon type and a once-per-short-rest Passage (spell-like effect). Learn more texts as you level
Keeper's Insight - Proficiency in History (expertise if already proficient)

1.name: Recitation
1.description: You learn 2 Recitations — short verbal invocations that function like cantrips. They require no material components and can be used at will. Recitations deal 1d8 damage (psychic, force, or radiant — chosen when learned), grant temporary hit points, or force saving throws. Damage scales: 2d8 at L5, 3d8 at L11, 4d8 at L17. Range: 60 feet for attacks, 30 feet for buffs.

1.name: Manifest Weapon
1.description: As a bonus action, you manifest a weapon from a text in your Library. The weapon appears in your hand, shimmering with narrative energy. You use your Charisma modifier for attack and damage rolls with manifested weapons. The weapon counts as magical, lasts 1 minute or until dismissed (no action required), and takes the form appropriate to its source text. You can only have one manifested weapon at a time (until L17). At L11, manifested weapons deal an extra 1d6 force, radiant, or psychic damage (chosen when you learn the text).

1.name: Keeper's Library
1.description: You maintain a Library of studied texts. You know 3 texts at L1, gaining more as you level. Each text grants two things: (1) A specific weapon type you can manifest, and (2) A Passage — a powerful effect you can invoke once per short rest by reciting a key line from the text. Passages use your Keeper save DC (8 + proficiency bonus + CHA modifier). When you gain a Keeper level, you can replace one text you know with a different one.

1.name: Keeper's Insight
1.description: You gain proficiency in History. If you are already proficient in History, you gain expertise instead (double your proficiency bonus for History checks).

2.name: Literary Recall
2.description: You can draw upon deep reserves of knowledge to re-invoke Passages you've already used. A number of times equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum 1) per long rest, you can use a Passage from one of your texts even if you've already expended it since your last short rest.

2.name: Keeper's Study
2.description: As a bonus action, you can focus your scholarly knowledge on one creature you can see within 60 feet, marking it as 'Studied' (proficiency bonus times per long rest, lasts 1 minute or until you study a different creature). While a creature is Studied: your Recitations and manifested weapon attacks deal an extra 1d4 damage to it (increases to 1d6 at L9, 1d8 at L15), and you learn one fact about it — its creature type, one resistance/vulnerability/immunity, or its highest ability score.

3.name: Genre Domain
3.description: You choose a Genre Domain — a literary genre that defines your scholarly specialization. Your Genre grants a passive benefit and one bonus text (added to your Texts Known, not counting against your limit). Choose from: History, Tactics, Romance, Poetry, Mythology, Political Science, Natural Philosophy, or Forbidden Texts. At L15, you choose a second Genre Domain or deepen your first with Genre Mastery.

5.name: Extra Attack
5.description: You can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

5.name: Eidetic Memory
5.description: Your mind becomes a perfect archive. You no longer need physical books to access your Library — all texts are perfectly recalled. You cannot be disarmed of your scholarly focus, your Library cannot be destroyed or stolen, and you have advantage on Intelligence checks to recall information from any text you have ever read (not just Library texts).

6.name: Keeper Specialization or Polymath
6.description: You choose one of two paths. SPECIALIZATION: Choose a subclass (Lorewarden, Mythslinger, Rhetorician, or Versebinder) that defines your combat role, gaining its L6 feature. OR POLYMATH: You embrace breadth over depth — gain proficiency in 2 additional skills, increase your Literary Recall uses by 2, and you can manifest weapons as a free action instead of a bonus action. A pure Keeper who chooses Polymath gains further improvements at L11 and L15.

7.name: Annotated Texts
7.description: Your deep study of your texts reveals hidden power. Once per turn when you hit a creature with a manifested weapon, you can add your Intelligence modifier to the damage roll.

9.name: Expanded Library
9.description: You unlock access to Rare texts — ancient, powerful works with stronger Passages and exotic weapon manifestations. When you learn a new text from this level onward, you can choose from the Rare text list in addition to the standard list.

10.name: Compelling Rhetoric
10.description: Once per short rest, you can use an action to speak with such authority that a creature within 60 feet that can hear and understand you must make a Wisdom saving throw against your Keeper save DC. On a failure, the creature is charmed or frightened (your choice) for 1 minute. The creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success.

11.name: Manifest Weapon Improvement
11.description: Your manifested weapons now deal an extra 1d6 damage on each hit. The damage type is force, radiant, or psychic (chosen when you learn the text that grants the weapon).

13.name: Living Text
13.description: Your manifested weapons take on a life of their own. Once per short rest, you can use one of the following: (1) Your manifested weapon makes an opportunity attack on its own when a hostile creature moves within its reach, using your attack modifier. (2) Your manifested weapon hovers defensively around you, granting you +1 AC until the start of your next turn.

14.name: Unwritten Knowledge
14.description: When you defeat a notable enemy (CR equal to or greater than your level) or discover a site of significant lore (DM's discretion), you can learn a new text inspired by the experience. This text is added to your Library and does not count against your Texts Known limit. You can hold a number of Unwritten texts equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum 1).

17.name: Masterwork Manifest
17.description: You can manifest TWO weapons simultaneously from different texts. Both weapons are active and you have access to both of their Passages. When you take the Attack action, you can attack once with each weapon. You can dismiss either weapon independently.

18.name: Keeper's Authority
18.description: Your knowledge commands respect. You have advantage on all Charisma checks related to knowledge, lore, intellectual discourse, or asserting authority through expertise. Additionally, creatures you are conversing with have disadvantage on Insight checks to determine if you are lying about scholarly or historical matters.

20.name: Living Library
20.description: Once per long rest, you can become the Library incarnate for 1 minute. During this time: you can switch your manifested weapon to any text in your Library without using an action; all of your expended Passages are immediately restored; your Recitations deal double damage; and you have resistance to psychic and force damage.

genreDomains.name: History
genreDomains.description: You specialize in chronicles, timelines, and the rise and fall of civilizations
genreDomains.passive: You have advantage on Intelligence checks to recall historical events, people, and places. When you use a Passage that targets an enemy, you can learn one piece of information about them (creature type, a resistance, or a vulnerability).
genreDomains.masteryCapstone: Once per long rest, you can declare a 'Lesson of the Past' — choose one creature you can see. For 1 minute, you and your allies have advantage on attack rolls against it as you recite its historical weaknesses.

bonusText.name: Chronicle of Fallen Empires
bonusText.passage: Declare one creature type (humanoid, undead, fiend, etc.). For 1 minute, your manifested weapons deal an extra 1d6 damage to creatures of that type.

genreDomains.name: Tactics
genreDomains.description: You specialize in military treatises, battle formations, and the art of war
genreDomains.passive: You add your Intelligence modifier to your initiative rolls. On the first round of combat, your manifested weapon attacks deal an extra 1d6 damage.
genreDomains.masteryCapstone: Once per long rest, you can issue a 'Battle Plan' — for 1 minute, up to 4 allies who can hear you add your Intelligence modifier to their initiative rolls (retroactively reordering if in combat) and gain advantage on their first attack each turn.

bonusText.name: The Art of the Decisive Blow
bonusText.passage: Choose up to 3 allies within 30 feet. Until the end of your next turn, those allies can add your Charisma modifier to their next attack roll.

genreDomains.name: Romance
genreDomains.description: You specialize in love epics, tragedies, and courtly tales of devotion and sacrifice
genreDomains.passive: You add your Charisma modifier as a bonus to Persuasion and Deception checks. When an ally within 30 feet is reduced to 0 HP, you can use your reaction to give them temporary HP equal to your Keeper level (once per short rest).
genreDomains.masteryCapstone: Once per long rest, you invoke a 'Lover's Vow' — choose one ally. For 1 minute, whenever that ally takes damage, you can choose to take half of it instead (no action required), and whenever you take damage, that ally can choose to take half of it instead.

bonusText.name: The Ballad of Twin Hearts
bonusText.passage: Choose one ally within 60 feet. For 1 minute, whenever you hit with a manifested weapon attack, that ally regains HP equal to your Charisma modifier.

genreDomains.name: Poetry
genreDomains.description: You specialize in verse, meter, rhythm, and the power of spoken word
genreDomains.passive: Your Recitations have their range doubled (120 feet for attacks, 60 feet for buffs). When you use the same Recitation on consecutive turns, its damage increases by 1d8 on the second use (resets if you switch or skip).
genreDomains.masteryCapstone: Once per long rest, you perform a 'Magnum Opus' — for 1 minute, all your Recitations deal maximum damage and their save DCs increase by 2.

bonusText.name: Verses of the First Song
bonusText.passage: You speak a cascading verse. Each creature of your choice within 30 feet must make a Wisdom save or be stunned until the end of your next turn.

genreDomains.name: Mythology
genreDomains.description: You specialize in creation myths, divine tales, and prophecy
genreDomains.passive: Choose a damage type when you select this Genre: fire, cold, lightning, or radiant. You gain resistance to that damage type. Your Passages that deal damage can deal that type instead of their normal type.
genreDomains.masteryCapstone: Once per long rest, you invoke a 'Mythic Invocation' — for 1 minute, your manifested weapons deal an extra 2d6 damage of your chosen type, and you gain immunity (instead of resistance) to that damage type.

bonusText.name: The Genesis Codex
bonusText.passage: You invoke a creation myth. Choose a point within 60 feet. A 20-foot radius burst of primordial energy erupts — each creature in the area makes a DEX save, taking 3d8 damage of your chosen type on a failure (half on success).

genreDomains.name: Political Science
genreDomains.description: You specialize in treatises on power, law, governance, and manipulation
genreDomains.passive: You gain expertise in Insight (double proficiency bonus). When you use Compelling Rhetoric (L10), the target has disadvantage on its initial saving throw.
genreDomains.masteryCapstone: Once per long rest, you issue an 'Edict of Authority' — choose up to 6 creatures within 60 feet that can hear you. Each must make a Wisdom save or be compelled to follow a one-sentence command (as the Command spell, but lasting 1 minute). Creatures can repeat the save at the end of each of their turns.

bonusText.name: Machiavelli's Treatise on Power
bonusText.passage: Choose one creature within 60 feet that can hear you. It must make a Wisdom save or regard one other creature of your choice as a trusted ally for 1 minute (redirecting its hostility if in combat).

genreDomains.name: Natural Philosophy
genreDomains.description: You specialize in bestiaries, herbalism, and elemental theory
genreDomains.passive: Your manifested weapons can deal fire, cold, lightning, or acid damage instead of their normal type (chosen each time you manifest). You have advantage on Nature and Survival checks.
genreDomains.masteryCapstone: Once per long rest, you invoke a 'Theorem of Elements' — for 1 minute, each time you hit with a manifested weapon, the target must make a CON save or suffer an elemental affliction: fire (ongoing 1d6 fire), cold (speed halved), lightning (can't take reactions), or acid (AC reduced by 2). Your choice each hit.

bonusText.name: Linnaeus's Bestiary of the Wild
bonusText.passage: Choose a creature you can see. You recall everything about its kind — for 1 minute, you know its AC, HP, resistances, vulnerabilities, and immunities. Your attacks against it score a critical hit on 19-20.

genreDomains.name: Forbidden Texts
genreDomains.description: You specialize in banned works, heretical writings, and truths too dangerous to be spoken freely
genreDomains.passive: Your Recitations and Passages can deal necrotic or psychic damage instead of their normal type. When you use a Passage, you can choose to take 1d6 necrotic damage (which can't be reduced) to increase the Passage's damage by 2d6 or its healing by 2d6.
genreDomains.masteryCapstone: Once per long rest, you open the 'Forbidden Chapter' — for 1 minute, your Passages cost no action to use (you can invoke one as part of an attack), but each Passage used deals 1d6 necrotic damage to you. Your Recitations deal an additional 2d8 necrotic damage.

bonusText.name: The Unnamed Codex
bonusText.passage: You speak a forbidden truth. Choose one creature within 60 feet — it must make an Intelligence save or take 4d8 psychic damage and be stunned until the end of your next turn. On a success, it takes half damage and isn't stunned.

subclasses.name: Lorewarden
subclasses.description: Tank and melee specialist who draws from protective texts and guardian myths, manifesting shields, wards, and heavy weapons to stand between danger and allies
subclasses.flavor: The Lorewarden is the scholar who read every account of every siege, every last stand, every oath kept unto death — and made those stories into armor. Where other Keepers recite from a distance, the Lorewarden steps forward, manifesting shields of narrative force and weapons heavy with the weight of legend. They are the ones who read about the defenders of Myth Drannor and thought: 'I can hold that line.' Often former knights, temple guardians, or dwarven sentinels who turned to scholarship, Lorewardens carry themselves with quiet authority. They don't need to raise their voice — the shield they conjure from the Fall of Myth Drannor speaks for them.
subclasses.quote: I have read how empires fall. I will not let this party be one of them.
subclasses.archetypeFeels: A knight who traded his commission for a library. The paladin who guards with knowledge instead of prayer. The scholar who survived the fall of a city because they'd already read how it would happen.

history.synergy: Learning enemy facts feeds your defensive positioning — know what's coming before it hits.

tactics.synergy: When you use Guardian's Manifest reaction on the first round of combat, your Tactics first-round bonus damage applies to the next ally attack against that attacker.

romance.synergy: Your protective reaction stacks with Romance's temp HP on ally drop — you prevent death and cushion the blow.

poetry.synergy: Doubled Recitation range is less useful for a melee defender, though consecutive bonus damage helps.

mythology.synergy: Resistance to a damage type plus your +2 AC shield makes you exceptionally durable against that element.

political_science.synergy: Insight expertise and Compelling Rhetoric help control enemies, but you're better at tanking than talking.

natural_philosophy.synergy: Elemental weapon types plus Guardian's Manifest — when you use Theorem of Elements, afflictions last 1 additional round while your shield is active.

forbidden_texts.synergy: Self-damage to boost Passages directly contradicts your role as the party's durable frontliner.

6.name: Guardian's Manifest
6.description: When you manifest a weapon, you can also manifest a shield of narrative energy, gaining +2 AC while the weapon is active. Additionally, when a creature within 5 feet of you hits an ally with an attack, you can use your reaction to impose disadvantage on the attack roll (before the DM says whether it hits). You can use this reaction a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus per long rest.

11.name: Bastion of Lore
11.description: While you have a manifested weapon, you and each ally within 10 feet of you gain a bonus to saving throws equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum +1). Additionally, when you use Extra Attack, you can replace one attack with a Passage invocation.

15.name: Saga of the Unbreakable
15.description: Once per long rest, when you or an ally within 30 feet would be reduced to 0 HP, you can invoke a legendary guardian tale. The target instead drops to 1 HP, gains temporary HP equal to your Keeper level + your Charisma modifier, and has resistance to all damage until the start of your next turn.

subclasses.name: Mythslinger
subclasses.description: Ranged striker who draws from hunter legends and marksman epics, manifesting legendary bows, crossbows, and thrown weapons to fight from a distance
subclasses.flavor: The Mythslinger read every story about the impossible shot — the arrow that split the moon, the bolt that pinned a dragon's shadow to the ground, the stone that felled a titan — and decided those stories were instruction manuals. Where other Keepers recite up close, the Mythslinger stands on a ridge half a mile away and lets the legends do the talking. They manifest bows strung with epic tension and crossbows loaded with narrative inevitability. Every shot carries the weight of a thousand hunting tales, and when a Mythslinger draws back, even the target knows — somewhere in a story, this already happened. Often former scouts, war archers, or tribal hunters who discovered that the best marksmanship guides were actually mythology, Mythslingers are patient, precise, and absolutely lethal at distances that shouldn't be possible.
subclasses.quote: There's a tale about a marksman who shot the wings off a stirge at six hundred paces. Probably a tall tale. I intend to find out.
subclasses.archetypeFeels: A ranger who hunts with legends instead of arrows. The sharpshooter who whispers myths before every kill shot. The researcher who left the library and never misses.

history.synergy: Learning enemy info at range helps you pick high-value targets and exploit vulnerabilities from safety.

tactics.synergy: On the first round of combat, Legendary Aim bonus damage applies to ALL attacks, not just one — devastating opening volley.

romance.synergy: Temp HP on ally drop and social bonuses don't help a ranged damage dealer fighting from 150 feet away.

poetry.synergy: Doubled Recitation range (120 ft) plus Legendary Aim range (150/600 ft) gives you unmatched reach for both attacks and utility.

mythology.synergy: When The Shot That Echoes crits, the AoE damage uses your Mythology chosen type instead of thunder. Mythic Invocation's +2d6 applies to every Legendary Aim shot.

political_science.synergy: Insight expertise and social debuffs don't help you shoot things from 600 feet away.

natural_philosophy.synergy: Elemental arrows at 150 ft range. Theorem of Elements afflictions on every hit creates a field of elemental devastation.

forbidden_texts.synergy: Self-damage is SAFE at 150 ft range — burn 1d6 HP for +2d6 Passage damage with nothing able to retaliate.

6.name: Legendary Aim
6.description: When you manifest a ranged weapon, its normal range becomes 150 feet and its long range becomes 600 feet. Once per turn, when you hit a creature with a manifested ranged weapon, you can deal an extra 1d8 damage. This extra damage increases to 2d8 at L11 and 3d8 at L15.

11.name: Volley of Legends
11.description: Once per short rest, you can invoke the tales of legendary archers. As an action, you make a ranged manifested weapon attack against each creature of your choice within a 30-foot radius of a point you can see within your weapon's range. Make a separate attack roll for each target.

15.name: The Shot That Echoes
15.description: Once per long rest, you fire a shot pulled from a myth so powerful it echoes through reality. Make a ranged manifested weapon attack against one creature. This attack has advantage and scores a critical hit on a roll of 17-20. On a hit, it deals an extra 6d8 force damage. Hit or miss, each creature within 15 feet of the target must make a DEX save against your Keeper DC or take 3d8 thunder damage.

subclasses.name: Rhetorician
subclasses.description: Controller and debuffer who draws from political texts and forbidden histories, using rhetoric to frighten, command, and compel
subclasses.flavor: The Rhetorician understood something the other Keepers missed: the most dangerous weapon in any story isn't the sword — it's the speech that starts the war. They studied the orations that toppled kingdoms, the arguments that broke treaties, the whispered words that turned allies into enemies. Where a Lorewarden uses stories as a shield and a Mythslinger uses them as ammunition, the Rhetorician uses them as a crowbar — prying open minds, wedging doubt into certainty, and leveraging fear into paralysis. They don't need to hurt you. They just need to make you hesitate, and hesitation in combat is death. Often former political advisors, guild negotiators, foreign diplomats, or spymasters who realized their words could literally reshape reality, Rhetoricians speak softly and carry the collected works of every tyrant, demagogue, and silver-tongued archdevil who ever lived.
subclasses.quote: There are books that drove men mad with a single reading. I only need a sentence.
subclasses.archetypeFeels: A politician's whisper given form and fury. The negotiator who never needed a blade. The spymaster who breaks enemy formations with a well-chosen phrase.

history.synergy: Learning enemy facts is nice but your debuffs work indiscriminately — you don't need to know weaknesses to exploit them.

tactics.synergy: Going first helps you lock enemies down before they act, but your control doesn't need the damage bonus.

romance.synergy: Temp HP on ally drop is reactive — a good controller prevents damage in the first place. Social bonuses are redundant with your existing rhetoric.

poetry.synergy: Bonus action Recitations at doubled range with consecutive stacking damage. Magnum Opus plus Words as Weapons is the ultimate control combo.

mythology.synergy: Resistance is nice for survivability but elemental damage doesn't serve your controller identity.

political_science.synergy: Insight expertise plus Compelling Rhetoric disadvantage. Creatures that fail Compelling Rhetoric also have disadvantage on their next save against your Rhetorician features.

natural_philosophy.synergy: Elemental weapon types and Nature/Survival are physical outdoor themes that don't serve a words-based controller.

forbidden_texts.synergy: Necrotic/psychic Recitations with self-damage boost. Risky for a squishy controller but the burst potential is real.

6.name: Words as Weapons
6.description: A number of times equal to your Charisma modifier per long rest, you can use a Recitation as a bonus action instead of an action. When a creature fails a saving throw against your Recitation or Passage, it has disadvantage on the next attack roll it makes before the end of its next turn. You also learn one additional Recitation.

11.name: Subjugating Rhetoric
11.description: Once per short rest, when you hit a creature with a manifested weapon or a creature fails a save against your Recitation, you can impose one of the following for 1 minute (WIS save at end of each turn to end): the creature's speed is halved; the creature cannot take reactions; or the creature must use its action to Dash away from you on its turn.

15.name: Forbidden Oration
15.description: Once per long rest, you deliver a speech so devastating it rewrites the battlefield. As an action, choose up to 3 hostile creatures within 60 feet that can hear you. Each must make a Wisdom save. On a failure, a creature is either paralyzed for 1 minute (can repeat save at end of each turn), or permanently loses the ability to speak for 24 hours (your choice per creature). Creatures immune to being charmed have advantage on this save.

subclasses.name: Versebinder
subclasses.description: Healer and support specialist who draws from sacred covenants and restoration myths, speaking binding words that mend wounds and bolster spirits
subclasses.flavor: The Versebinder found the stories that end with 'and they were healed.' Every culture has them — the prayer that closed the wound, the hymn that cured the plague, the lullaby that called the dying back from the threshold. Where other Keepers weaponize narrative, the Versebinder remembers that the oldest stories were medicines, spoken over the sick and the broken to make them whole again. They manifest not swords but sutures, not shields but salves, weaving prose so restorative it literally knits flesh and mends bone. Often former temple healers, monks who turned from prayer to prose, or scholarly scribes who discovered their words could do more than move hearts — they could restart them. Versebinders are the ones the party doesn't appreciate until they're bleeding out and hearing a gentle voice reciting the only story that matters: the one where you survive.
subclasses.quote: Every story about death has a sequel. Let me read you the one where you get back up.
subclasses.archetypeFeels: A monk who heals with scripture instead of laying on hands. The priest whose hymns close wounds as surely as any spell. The scribe who writes the ending where everyone lives.

history.synergy: Learning enemy info helps you advise the party but doesn't directly boost your healing output.

tactics.synergy: Going first lets you pre-buff with Passages before enemies act. First-round damage is wasted on a healer, but initiative matters.

romance.synergy: When Mending Verse heals an ally at or below half HP, they also gain temp HP equal to your CHA mod. Lover's Vow damage sharing plus your revive makes allies nearly unkillable.

poetry.synergy: Doubled Recitation range helps you buff from safety, but you're spending turns healing, not stacking consecutive damage.

mythology.synergy: Resistance helps you survive, but elemental damage doesn't serve your support role.

political_science.synergy: Insight expertise helps read situations but Compelling Rhetoric competes with your action economy for healing.

natural_philosophy.synergy: Advantage on Nature/Survival helps with exploration. Elemental weapon switching gives combat versatility when you're not healing.

forbidden_texts.synergy: Spending HP to boost Passages directly contradicts your role as the party's healer — you can't heal others if you're killing yourself.

6.name: Mending Verse
6.description: When you use a Passage, you can also heal one creature within 30 feet for 1d8 + your Charisma modifier HP. This healing increases to 2d8 + CHA at L11 and 3d8 + CHA at L15. Additionally, when you use Literary Recall to re-invoke a Passage, the creature healed by Mending Verse also gains temporary HP equal to your Keeper level.

11.name: Covenant of Restoration
11.description: Once per long rest, you recite a binding covenant. Choose up to 6 creatures within 30 feet. Each regains HP equal to 2d8 + your Charisma modifier and is cured of one condition (blinded, deafened, frightened, poisoned, or stunned). For the next minute, those creatures have advantage on saving throws against being frightened or charmed.

15.name: The Verse That Cannot Be Unwritten
15.description: Once per long rest, when a creature within 60 feet that you can see dies (drops to 0 HP and fails all death saves, or is killed outright), you can use your reaction to speak a verse of such power that it binds the creature's soul to their body. The creature is restored to 1 HP and gains temporary HP equal to your Keeper level + your Charisma modifier. This cannot bring back a creature that has been dead for more than 1 round.

6.name: Polymath
6.description: You gain proficiency in 2 additional skills of your choice. Your Literary Recall uses per long rest increase by 2. You can manifest weapons as a free action instead of a bonus action.

11.name: Polymath: Broad Study
11.description: You learn 2 additional texts from any Genre (even Genres you haven't chosen as your Genre Domain). These don't count against your Texts Known. Once per short rest, you can switch your manifested weapon to a different text's weapon without dismissing it first (no action required).

15.name: Polymath: Renaissance Scholar
15.description: Once per long rest, you can invoke any Genre Domain's passive benefit for 1 minute, even if you haven't chosen that Genre. Additionally, all your Passages gain a bonus to their damage, healing, or save DCs equal to your Charisma modifier.

monk.name: Monk
monk.description: A master of martial arts who turned their own body into a weapon. You move faster than the eye, strike where it hurts most, and need nothing but discipline to do it.
toolProficiencies: Choose one type of artisan's tools or one musical instrument
features: Unarmored Defense - While not wearing armor or wielding a shield, your AC equals 10 + DEX modifier + WIS modifier
Martial Arts - Your practice of martial arts gives you mastery of unarmed strikes and monk weapons
Monk's Focus - You harness Focus Points, equal to your Monk level, to fuel Flurry of Blows, Patient Defense, Step of the Wind, and other features

subclasses.name: Way of the Open Hand
subclasses.description: Master of unarmed combat techniques

3.name: Open Hand Technique
3.description: Whenever you hit a creature with one of the attacks granted by your Flurry of Blows, you can impose one of the following effects on that target: It must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or be knocked prone. It must make a Strength saving throw. If it fails, you can push it up to 15 feet away from you. It can't take reactions until the end of your next turn.

6.name: Wholeness of Body
6.description: You gain the ability to heal yourself. As an action, you can regain hit points equal to three times your monk level. You must finish a long rest before you can use this feature again.

11.name: Tranquility
11.description: You can enter a special meditation that surrounds you with an aura of peace. At the end of a long rest, you gain the effect of a Sanctuary spell that lasts until the start of your next long rest (the spell can end early as normal). The saving throw DC for the spell equals 8 + your Wisdom modifier + your proficiency bonus.

17.name: Quivering Palm
17.description: You gain the ability to set up lethal vibrations in someone's body. When you hit a creature with an unarmed strike, you can spend 3 ki points to start these imperceptible vibrations, which last for a number of days equal to your monk level. The vibrations are harmless unless you use your action to end them. When you use this action, the creature must make a Constitution saving throw. If it fails, it is reduced to 0 hit points. If it succeeds, it takes 10d10 necrotic damage.

subclasses.name: Way of Shadow
subclasses.description: Ninja-like warrior who uses stealth and shadow magic

3.name: Shadow Arts
3.description: You can use your ki to duplicate the effects of certain spells. As an action, you can spend 2 ki points to cast Darkness, Darkvision, Pass without Trace, or Silence, without providing material components. Additionally, you gain the Minor Illusion cantrip if you don't already know it.

6.name: Shadow Step
6.description: You gain the ability to step from one shadow into another. When you are in dim light or darkness, as a bonus action you can teleport up to 60 feet to an unoccupied space you can see that is also in dim light or darkness. You then have advantage on the first melee attack you make before the end of the turn.

11.name: Cloak of Shadows
11.description: You have learned to become one with the shadows. When you are in an area of dim light or darkness, you can use your action to become invisible. You remain invisible until you make an attack, cast a spell, or are in an area of bright light.

17.name: Opportunist
17.description: You can exploit a creature's momentary distraction when it is hit by an attack. Whenever a creature within 5 feet of you is hit by an attack made by a creature other than you, you can use your reaction to make a melee attack against that creature.

subclasses.name: Way of the Four Elements
subclasses.description: Channel the elements through ki

3.name: Disciple of the Elements
3.description: You learn magical disciplines that harness the power of the four elements. Some disciplines require you to spend ki points when you use them. You learn the Elemental Attunement discipline and one other elemental discipline of your choice. You learn one additional elemental discipline of your choice at 6th, 11th, and 17th level. Whenever you learn a new elemental discipline, you can also replace one elemental discipline that you already know with a different discipline.

6.name: Additional Discipline
6.description: You learn one additional elemental discipline of your choice.

11.name: Additional Discipline
11.description: You learn one additional elemental discipline of your choice.

17.name: Additional Discipline
17.description: You learn one additional elemental discipline of your choice.

subclasses.name: Way of the Sun Soul
subclasses.description: Radiant soul who channels divine light

3.name: Radiant Sun Bolt
3.description: You gain a new attack option that you can use with the Attack action. This special attack is a ranged spell attack with a range of 30 feet. You are proficient with it, and you add your Dexterity modifier to its attack and damage rolls. Its damage is radiant, and its damage die is a d4. This die changes as you gain monk levels, as shown in the Martial Arts column of the Monk table. When you take the Attack action on your turn and use this special attack as part of it, you can spend 1 ki point to make the special attack twice as a bonus action.

6.name: Searing Arc Strike
6.description: You gain the ability to channel your ki into searing waves of energy. Immediately after you take the Attack action on your turn, you can spend 2 ki points to cast the Burning Hands spell as a bonus action. You can spend additional ki points to cast Burning Hands as a higher-level spell. Each additional ki point you spend increases the spell's level by 1. The maximum number of ki points (2 plus any additional points) that you can spend on the spell equals half your monk level.

11.name: Searing Sunburst
11.description: You gain the ability to create an orb of light that erupts into a devastating explosion. As an action, you magically create an orb and hurl it at a point you choose within 150 feet, where it erupts into a sphere of radiant light for a brief but deadly instant. Each creature in that 20-foot-radius sphere must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or take 2d6 radiant damage. A creature doesn't need to make the save if the creature is behind total cover that is opaque. You can increase the sphere's damage by spending ki points. Each point you spend, to a maximum of 3, increases the damage by 2d6.

17.name: Sun Shield
17.description: You become wreathed in a luminous, magical aura. You shed bright light in a 30-foot radius and dim light for an additional 30 feet. You can extinguish or restore the light as a bonus action. If a creature hits you with a melee attack while this light shines, you can use your reaction to deal radiant damage to the creature. The radiant damage equals 5 + your Wisdom modifier.

subclasses.name: Way of the Drunken Master
subclasses.description: Unpredictable fighter using drunken techniques

3.name: Bonus Proficiencies
3.description: You gain proficiency in the Performance skill if you don't already have it. Your martial arts technique mixes combat training with the precision of a dancer and the antics of a jester. You also gain proficiency with brewer's supplies if you don't already have it.

3.name: Drunken Technique
3.description: You learn how to twist and turn quickly as part of your Flurry of Blows. Whenever you use Flurry of Blows, you gain the benefit of the Disengage action, and your walking speed increases by 10 feet until the end of the current turn.

6.name: Tipsy Sway
6.description: You can move in sudden, swaying ways. You gain the following benefits: Leap to Your Feet (when you're prone, you can stand up by spending 5 feet of movement, rather than half your speed), Redirect Attack (when a creature misses you with a melee attack roll, you can spend 1 ki point as a reaction to cause that attack to hit one creature of your choice, other than the attacker, that you can see within 5 feet of you).

11.name: Drunkard's Luck
11.description: You always seem to get a lucky bounce at the right moment. When you make an ability check, an attack roll, or a saving throw and have disadvantage on the roll, you can spend 2 ki points to cancel the disadvantage for that roll.

17.name: Intoxicated Frenzy
17.description: You gain the ability to make an overwhelming number of attacks against a group of enemies. When you use your Flurry of Blows, you can make up to three additional attacks with it (up to a total of five Flurry of Blows attacks), provided that each Flurry of Blows attack targets a different creature this turn.

subclasses.name: Way of the Kensei
subclasses.description: Master of weapons as extensions of the body

3.name: Path of the Kensei
3.description: Your special martial arts training leads you to master the use of certain weapons. Choose two types of weapons to be your kensei weapons: one melee weapon and one ranged weapon. Each of these weapons can be any simple or martial weapon that lacks the heavy and special properties. You gain the following benefits while wielding kensei weapons: Agile Parry (+2 AC if you make an unarmed strike and are holding a kensei melee weapon), Kensei's Shot (bonus action to add 1d4 damage to ranged attacks this turn), Way of the Brush (you gain proficiency with calligrapher's supplies or painter's supplies).

6.name: One with the Blade
6.description: You extend your ki into your kensei weapons, granting you the following benefits: Magic Kensei Weapons (your attacks with your kensei weapons count as magical for the purpose of overcoming resistance and immunity to nonmagical attacks and damage), Deft Strike (when you hit a target with a kensei weapon, you can spend 1 ki point to cause the weapon to deal extra damage to the target equal to your Martial Arts die).

11.name: Sharpen the Blade
11.description: You gain the ability to augment your weapons further with your ki. As a bonus action, you can expend up to 3 ki points to grant one kensei weapon you touch a bonus to attack and damage rolls when you attack with it. The bonus equals the number of ki points you spent. This bonus lasts for 1 minute or until you use this feature again. This feature has no effect on a magic weapon that already has a bonus to attack and damage rolls.

17.name: Unerring Accuracy
17.description: Your mastery of weapons grants you extraordinary accuracy. If you miss with an attack roll using a monk weapon on your turn, you can reroll it. You can use this feature only once on each of your turns.

subclasses.name: Way of Mercy
subclasses.description: Masked healer who brings life or death

3.name: Implements of Mercy
3.description: You gain proficiency in the Insight and Medicine skills, and you gain proficiency with the herbalism kit. You also gain a special mask, which you often wear when using the features of this subclass.

3.name: Hand of Healing
3.description: Your mystical touch can mend wounds. As an action, you can spend 1 ki point to touch a creature and restore a number of hit points equal to a roll of your Martial Arts die + your Wisdom modifier. When you use your Flurry of Blows, you can replace one of the unarmed strikes with a use of this feature without spending a ki point for the healing.

3.name: Hand of Harm
3.description: You use your ki to inflict wounds. When you hit a creature with an unarmed strike, you can spend 1 ki point to deal extra necrotic damage equal to one roll of your Martial Arts die + your Wisdom modifier. You can use this feature only once per turn.

6.name: Physician's Touch
6.description: You can administer even greater cures with a touch, and if you feel it's necessary, you can use your knowledge to cause harm. When you use Hand of Healing on a creature, you can also end one disease or one of the following conditions affecting the creature: blinded, deafened, paralyzed, poisoned, or stunned. When you use Hand of Harm on a creature, you can subject that creature to the poisoned condition until the end of your next turn.

11.name: Flurry of Healing and Harm
11.description: You can now mete out a flurry of comfort and hurt. When you use Flurry of Blows, you can now replace each of the unarmed strikes with a use of your Hand of Healing, without spending ki points for the healing. In addition, when you make an unarmed strike with Flurry of Blows, you can use Hand of Harm with that strike without spending the ki point for Hand of Harm. You can still use Hand of Harm only once per turn.

17.name: Hand of Ultimate Mercy
17.description: Your mastery of life energy opens the door to the ultimate mercy. As an action, you can touch the corpse of a creature that died within the past 24 hours and expend 5 ki points.
